**People › Cleaners: the old Cleaners roster's per-cleaner figures.** New columns Customer rating, Reliability, Attendance and Hours, 30 d (`components/v2/admin/accounts/hub/accounts-columns.tsx`, in Columns; Customer rating and Reliability shown by default on the Cleaners tab, Attendance and Hours one click away; hidden by default on every other tab and in the old Accounts hub; "Show all columns" now really shows all). Server sorts `rating`, `reliability`, `attendance`, `hours30` (`lib/accounts/list/types.ts` `ACCOUNT_SORTS`, `derive.ts` `sortValue`; a missing figure sorts last both ways; an unknown sort is still 400, and these sorts are 400 for a viewer without the figures). ## Owner decisions: sensitive void and credit notes, revocable invitations, assistant team moves, Message team, folding figures, laundry Today (2026-11-13)

Six owner decisions of 2026-11-13. Left uncommitted in the working tree. One forward migration, `20261113050000_invitation_revoked`.

**1. Void and credit notes is a sensitive action.** In `lib/rbac/capabilities.ts` `invoices.void_credit` moved from tier `manage` to tier `full` with `sensitiveAction: "invoices.void_credit"` (new key in `lib/security/sensitive-actions.ts` and `SENSITIVE_ACTION_CAPABILITY`). An operations manager needs Finance at Full or the explicit sensitive grant (person, then custom preset), as for the other eight sensitive grants; administrators always have it. Enforced on the server on every route that voids or creates a credit note: `PATCH /api/admin/invoices/[id]` with `status: "VOID"` (voids an invoice or a credit note) and `POST /api/admin/invoices/[id]/credit-note`. Order: live role guard, `capabilityRefusal` (403 `CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` before any credential is read), then the acting person's own PIN through `voidCreditSecurityRefusal` (`lib/billing/client-invoice-void-guard.ts` → `verifyInvoiceSecurity(…, "invoices.void_credit")` → `verifySensitiveAction`): 403 while testing as someone, 423 for a missing, wrong or locked PIN, the one-time password-plus-new-PIN setup as elsewhere. Administrators are prompted for their own PIN exactly as on the other sensitive actions (verifySensitiveAction checks the PIN for ADMIN too; only the capability check is skipped). There is no bulk void or bulk credit note (`CLIENT_INVOICE_BULK_ACTIONS` is approve / send / approve-and-send / Xero push), so no bulk path exists to guard; the Xero "Reconcile / void" route keeps its own sensitive grant `invoices.correct`. UI: the Void and Issue credit note dialogs use `EConfirmModal requireSecurity` (the shared own-PIN prompt, `own-pin-fields.tsx`) and send `{ security }`; the list (`GET /api/admin/invoices?paginated=1` answers `canVoidCredit`) and the editor (`canVoidCredit` on the editor data) show Void and Issue credit note disabled with the reason ("Void and credit notes is a sensitive action: it needs Finance at Full (or that grant) and your own PIN. Ask an administrator.") for someone without it; "New invoice → Credit note" says the same. The Access screen shows the capability with the Sensitive badge under Finance and "What X can do" reads "Void invoices and raise credit notes (asked for their own PIN)" (both catalog-driven). **What changes after deploy:** every operations manager who could void or raise credit notes at Finance Manage loses it until an administrator sets Finance to Full or grants "Void and credit notes" to them; administrators keep it and are asked for their PIN. The parity test records this as its one intended change (`INTENDED_CHANGES`, comment naming the owner decision and 2026-11-13).

**2. Invitations are revocable.** `UserInvitation` (account and assistant invitations are the same row) gains `revokedAt` and `revokedById` (FK to User, ON DELETE SET NULL; no data change). `lib/accounts/invitation-revoke.ts`: same senders as Resend invitation (`resolveAccountEmailActor`: ADMIN, or OPS_MANAGER with Staff accounts at Manage; never while testing as someone; never on oneself; never on a higher role, 403), only an invitation neither accepted nor already withdrawn (409 with the reason; an expired one may be revoked), a conditional `updateMany` in one transaction with the audit row `ACCOUNT_INVITATION_REVOKED` (actor, `actorRole`, never the token). Routes: `POST /api/admin/users/[id]/account-emails/revoke-invitation` and bulk `POST /api/admin/users/account-emails/revoke { userIds }` (≤ 50, per-row revoked / refused with reason). Accepting: one pure state rule `lib/auth/invitation-state.ts` (invalid, accepted, revoked, expired, inactive, valid) shared by `/accept-invite/[token]` ("Invitation withdrawn · This invitation was withdrawn. Ask the office for a new one.") and `GET/POST /api/auth/accept-invite/[token]` (410 with `code: "REVOKED"`); the accept POST now claims the invitation with a conditional update (same token, not accepted, not revoked, not expired) in the transaction that sets the password, so a revoke racing an accept leaves exactly one outcome (DB-tested). Resend after a revoke issues a fresh invitation as before (`createUserInvitation` clears the revoked fields); the copy-link route refuses a withdrawn invitation. Screens: People › Invitations rows menu "Revoke invitation", the detail panel (Account emails section "Revoke invitation" and history line "Invitation withdrawn"), bulk "Revoke N" (only selected rows with a pending invitation), a "Revoked" state chip and an Expires cell "Revoked <date>"; a revoked row offers "New invite". People › Assistants rows: "Revoke invite" for invited / expired members, new status "Invite withdrawn" with "New invite". Every revoke is confirmed in `components/v2/admin/people/revoke-invitation-dialog.tsx` (labelled, focus-trapped `EActionDialog`).

**3. Moving an assistant between teams of the same client.** `lib/va/move-member.ts` (one transaction, row lock on the login, conditional update on the old team): refuses a login that is not an assistant on a team (404), an unknown team (404), the same team, another client's team (`CROSS_CLIENT`, "Assistants can only move between teams of the same client. Invite a new login for the other client instead.") and a switched-off team unless confirmed (`DESTINATION_INACTIVE`); audited `MOVE_VA_MEMBER` with `before` / `after` team, grants and scope, actor, role and impersonator. Pure rules and the "Loses: … Gains: …" / property sentence: `lib/va/move-rules.ts`. Route `PATCH /api/admin/va-teams/[id]/members/[userId] { toTeamId, confirmInactive? }` (the path's team must still be the assistant's; 409 otherwise). Rights: administrators only (`requireRole([ADMIN])`), matching the Assistants screen's other team changes (remove from team, delete team) and the screen's `canManage`; note the existing team PATCH route also lets an operations manager with the clients pack edit grants, which was left unchanged. Access follows the team from the person's next request: `requireClientPortal` and `resolvePortalScopeForUser` re-read `User.vaTeamId`, the team's grants and its scope from the database on every call and the session token carries none of it (DB-tested). UI: "Move to team…" in the Assistants row menu and in the team panel's Members tab (`components/v2/admin/people/assistants/move-team-dialog.tsx`: only the same client's other teams, the change stated, a tick for a switched-off team, frozen while moving, failed move kept).

**4. Message team on a job.** The admin job page's "Message team" primary action (ASSIGNED, EN_ROUTE, IN_PROGRESS, PAUSED) opens `components/v2/admin/jobs/detail/message-team-dialog.tsx` instead of linking to the compose page. Disabled with the reason when nobody is assigned ("Nobody is assigned to this job yet, so there is no team to message. Assign a cleaner first.") or when the viewer may not send (`primaryActionFor` `teamMessage`, filled by the server page from `officeSendDecision(session, "job_team_message")`). Recipients: the cleaners assigned now, by name, each removable, none addable. Message ≤ 600 characters. Transports with the shared `TransportChoice` (now catalog-driven; `JOB_MESSAGE_CATALOG`: Inbox default, Push, SMS), each disabled with its reason (type switched off, SMS not configured, no assigned cleaner with a phone); "Don't ask again" uses `office_send_transports_v1` kind `job_office_message` (`lib/notifications/send-transport-kinds.ts`; listed in Notifications › Preferences › Your sending choices). Server: `lib/notifications/job-office-message.ts` behind `GET`/`POST /api/admin/jobs/[id]/office-message` with `requireOfficeSend("job_team_message")` (ADMIN, or OPS_MANAGER with the Jobs pack at Manage, new manage-tier capability `jobs.team_message`; never while impersonating). Ids not assigned are refused with the reason; Inbox/Push go through `sendOfficeNotification` with scope `JOB_ASSIGNED_CLEANER` (re-checked at queue and dispatch), the job id and `/cleaner/jobs/<id>` link; SMS goes through the SMS chokepoint after re-checking the scope immediately before the provider call, once per request key (`dispatchNotificationOnce`). Results per person and transport: accepted / skipped / failed with the reason, never delivered. One send per `idempotencyKey` (a repeat answers the recorded outcomes with `replayed: true`); limits 30 per sender per hour (in-process and audit count) and 12 per job per day. Audit `JOB_OFFICE_MESSAGE_SENT` on the job (shown in its History) with actor, role, text, title, recipients, transports, outcomes. Catalog `job.office_message` (Cleaners; SMS marked `directTransports` so no outbox banner applies) and editable wording (`definitions/actions.ts`: Inbox title "Message from the office: {{jobLabel}}", body "{{messageText}}"; SMS "sNeek office ({{jobLabel}}): {{messageText}}").

**5. Figures fold on a phone.** One shared component, `components/v2/ui/collapsible-figures.tsx`: below 640px the tiles start collapsed behind one labelled disclosure button ("10 figures · Show", `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`); from 640px the button is hidden and the tiles show exactly as before (the wrapper takes their container's place and spacing). Used on every People tab with figures (Clients, Cleaners, Invitations through `FactStrip collapsible`), Invoices and pay › Client invoices (5 figures), Pay runs (3 figures under the 2 KPI tiles, 5 cards stacked) and the Quality hub (6 cards). Checked and left as they are: Properties (4 cards), Cleaner invoices (4), Jobs list, Approvals and Urgent stock (no figure tiles above the list on a phone).

A run scheduled today that failed today is FLAGGED with today's date and shows, marked Flagged. ## Tone band replaces the coloured left line (owner decision, 2026-11-13)

Visual change only: no behaviour, data, permission or wording change; no schema change. The owner disliked the coloured vertical line on flagged cards and rows and chose design B, the tinted title band, in colour set 1 "Honey and wine".

**Tokens.** `app/v2/estate.css` gains `--e-band-{attention,problem,good,info}-{bg,line,fg,muted,pill}` for light and Obsidian dark. Light values are set 1 exactly; dark keeps the hues with low-lightness tints and light text. Every text pair is WCAG AA or better (light: title on band 9.5 to 10.6:1, secondary 5.5 to 5.9:1, pill on surface 8.0 to 9.3:1; dark: title 11.5 to 11.8:1, secondary 7.5 to 7.8:1, pill on surface 8.8 to 11.1:1).

**Primitive.** `components/v2/ui/tone-band.tsx` (plain module, no hooks, importable by server pages): `ETone`, `toneBandClass`, `toneNoticeClass`, `tonePillClass`, `toneMutedClass`, `toneRowCellClass`, `toneFromLegacy`, `E_BAND_BADGE_CLASS`, and `EToneCard`, `EToneBand`, `EToneRowCell`, `EToneNotice`, `ETonePill`. `EAlert` (primitives) now uses the notice tint with a hairline border, so every caller follows. `EDataTable`'s active row keeps its soft primary tint and loses the inset left line.

**Converted.** About 45 v2 files across admin, cleaner, client, laundry, QA, maintenance, login and onboarding: inline notices become tinted boxes (warning → attention, danger → problem, success → good, info → info; champagne "important request" and "new feedback" accents → attention); flagged cards put their title row in the band with the existing badge on the surface colour (cleaner offer card, open coaching records, unseen QA feedback, client "approvals waiting", laundry partner "warning" office requests); client calendar chips keep their status tint without the line. Cards that were always lined but have nothing to flag (acknowledged coaching, seen QA feedback) are now plain.

**Left alone deliberately.** Column dividers and drawer edges (`border-l` 1px, `border-l-0`), segmented-control separators, maintenance and handoff history timelines, the job timeline connector, the form renderer's nested-question guide, the public blog lead quote, and (until the pay-request fix converted it to `toneNoticeClass("attention")`, 2026-11-13) `components/v2/cleaner/pay-requests-panel.tsx`. No accents were found under the approvals paths.

**Rules and tests.** `docs/style/operational-ui.md`, "Flagged cards, rows and notices: the tone band". `tests/components/tone-band.test.tsx` (tone to classes, card / row / notice shapes, plain card has no band, EAlert) and `tests/lib/no-left-accent-lines.test.ts` (scan of `components/v2` and `app/v2` with an explicit allowlist).

## Cleaner pay is the requested amount, not the client charge (owner rule, 2026-11-13)

Owner rule: "When cleaners request money we will send it to clients as needed with a different rate, and once the client approved, cleaners only get paid whatever they requested only, not the full approved amount." No schema change.

**Two amounts, kept apart.** A pay request (`CleanerPayAdjustment`) holds the CLEANER PAY: `requestedAmount` (what the cleaner asked for) and `approvedAmount` (what they are paid; payroll and cleaner invoices read only this, through `lib/finance/pay-adjustments.ts`). Sending it to the client creates a client approval record (AppSetting `client_approvals_v1`, `metadata.source = "pay_adjustment"`) whose `amount` (or `counterAmount` while a counter-offer is open; accepting a counter writes it into `amount`) is the CLIENT CHARGE. The two were already stored separately; the bug was in reading them. `normalizePayAdjustmentAmounts` (`lib/pay-adjustments/display.ts`) set `primaryDisplayAmount` to the client amount once a client approval existed, and every approve field pre-filled from it: the Approvals decision panel and list one-click Approve (`payAskedAmount` in `lib/admin/approvals/rows.ts`), bulk "Approve as asked" (`planPayApprovals`, which also checked `expectedAmounts` against it), Finance › Pay adjustments review (`primaryAmount`) and the classic pay requests workspace (`getPrimaryAmount`). There was no automatic path: a client's approval never approves the cleaner's pay by itself; the office still decides it.

**Rules now.** One plain module, `lib/payroll/cleaner-pay-amount.ts`:
- `primaryDisplayAmount` / `payAskedAmount` / `cleanerPayFieldDefault` are always the requested amount, before and after the client's answer, after a counter-offer and after a reload. A missing requested amount is null ("No amount recorded"), never $0.00.
- The client charge is shown beside the pay field, read only, from `clientChargeView`: "Client charge approved: $60.00", "Client counter-offer: $50.00", "Client charge awaiting approval: $60.00". The decision panel field is labelled "Pay the cleaner ($)".
- Server (`decideCleanerPayAmount`, enforced in `PATCH /api/admin/pay-adjustments/[id]` for approve and approved-amount edits, and in the Decided tab's Change amount, `POST /api/admin/approvals/history/[id]`, pay-request queue only): no amount sent → the requested amount; at or below the request → allowed as before (no new note requirement); above the request → 403 `ABOVE_REQUEST` unless the caller holds ADMIN in a real session (not "test as") and sends `overrideAboveRequest: true` with `overrideReason` (the Decided tab uses its required note as the reason) — 400 `OVERRIDE_REASON_REQUIRED` without one. An override writes an `AuditLog` row `PAY_ADJUSTMENT_PAID_ABOVE_REQUEST` (actor id, actor role, requested amount, paid amount, reason) and the decision's own audit row carries `aboveRequestOverride`. Rectifications and bonuses (their own queues) are not cleaner requests and are unchanged.
- Bulk "Approve as asked" approves each row at the cleaner's requested amount and refuses a row whose confirmed amount differs from it.
- The client charge is only read by these paths; the client approval record is never changed by a cleaner pay decision. No client invoice code reads client approvals, so invoicing is unchanged.
- The cleaner's routes, Pay page and job screen never read the client approval (source scan in `tests/lib/cleaner-pay-amount.test.ts`); they show requested and approved pay only.

**Existing records are not rewritten.** `lib/payroll/paid-above-request.ts` (`listPaidAboveRequest`) and the read-only `scripts/review-paid-above-request.ts` list approved, unpaid pay requests whose approved amount is above the request. Approvals › Decided has a "Paid above request" chip (`?paidAboveRequest=1` on the history route) and marks such rows "Paid above request (asked $X)". The SQL is in the review record.

**Also in this change.** The cleaner Pay requests list's "From the office" note uses the shared tinted notice `toneNoticeClass("attention")` instead of a gold left line (its pending allowlist entry is removed from `tests/lib/no-left-accent-lines.test.ts`).

**Tests.** New: `tests/lib/cleaner-pay-amount.test.ts`, `tests/api/pay-adjustment-cleaner-pay-rule.test.ts`, `tests/components/pay-request-cleaner-amount.test.tsx`, `tests/db/cleaner-pay-requested-amount.test.ts` (PostgreSQL 55439). Changed on purpose: `tests/lib/approvals-bulk-pay.test.ts` (the "uses the client-approved amount" case now asserts the requested amount), `tests/api/pay-adjustment-settlement-guards.test.ts` (its race and notification cases edited the amount to $25 on a $20 request, now refused; they use $15 so they still test what they were written for).
