## Scheduling rules: visible, locked, versioned (2026-11-14)

Owner request: "make it visible to view the laundry auto scheduling rules, make it able to changeable as needed, also do the same to jobs auto scheduling rules that we currently hard coded; do not change any rules at all as they are exactly as I need. Also keep them safe and locked, also enable to have backups on these critical settings, also undo any accidental changes or restore previous versions."

**Nothing changed by default.** Every hard-coded scheduling literal moved unchanged into `lib/scheduling-rules/constants.ts` and the modules that used it import it (planner, key-lost, clean start, laundry reminders and route, iCal sync, turnover readiness, priority, auto-pause, stale en route, day reminders, dispatch, missed clock-in, unfinished reminders, client task auto-approve, deep clean, cleaner laundry fallback). `lib/gps/departure.ts` keeps its own literals (another session owns it); the parity test pins them to the copies. Version 1 of the rules is "Original (current behaviour)": the original literals for rules that were in code and the LIVE stored settings for rules that were settings. It is created the first time anything reads the rules (the worker, an iCal sync, the planner, or the screen), never by the migration, so code defaults can never overwrite values the owner had saved. A stored field that the settings row does not carry takes the value `sanitizeSettings` already used for it (`SETTINGS_FIELD_DEFAULTS`, pinned to `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`), which is the value the engine was already running on; such fields are listed on the seed audit row.

**Registry** (`lib/scheduling-rules/registry.ts`, plain module). 82 rules in plain words, each with its kind: changeable (45 values in `values.ts`, four of them the stored-but-not-used fields), fixed logic (shown with its value), not applied (weekends and public holidays, mid-stay cleans, offer expiry) and stored-but-not-used (`laundryOperations.pickupCutoffTime`, `defaultPickupTime`, `defaultDropoffTime`, `routeOptimization.enabled`). Quirks are documented and kept: a cancelled job still counts as the "next clean" and as a same-day iCal conflict; the recurring window starts on the UTC date; the planner's dates depend on the process time zone (docker-compose sets `TZ=Australia/Sydney`, the Dockerfile alone does not); `maxOutdoorDays` drives both the planner cap and the over-turnaround exception; the expected-finish display for a job with no due time keeps the original 15:00. Changeable code values now read by the engine: pickup offset, minimum turnaround, back-to-back and micro-cycle limits, buffer flag, key-lost times, default clean start (plan brief), driver-nudge picked-up hours, turnover ready-by time, auto-pause hours, stale en-route hours, day-reminder unlock hour and lead. Fixed in code and shown read-only: priority thresholds, admin attention 48 h, nudge cool-down, route model, missed clock-in, client task auto-approve lead, unfinished-job dedup, deep-clean cadence, dispatch constants, GPS departure, iCal technical limits, worker cron times.

**Store** (`SchedulingRuleVersion`, `SchedulingRuleSnapshot`; migration `20261114010000_scheduling_rule_versions`, additive). Versions are never edited or deleted; restore and import create new versions. Each row carries the canonical values, a sha256 checksum, the rules format, an effective day (Sydney date key, live from midnight), `appliesToExisting`, reason, actor and `activatedAt`. `loadSchedulingRuleBook` (`store.ts`) validates every row (format, bounds, unknown keys, checksum) and throws `SchedulingRulesUnavailableError` otherwise: the planner, the iCal job sync (rules read before anything is written, run recorded ERROR) and the four worker sweeps stop with the reason; nothing falls back to code defaults. Seeding and activation run under the advisory lock `scheduling-rules`.

**Which version applies** (`book.ts`). New runs and new jobs, and every run-time check, use the live version (highest version already effective). An existing laundry run or iCal turnover keeps the version that was live when it was created unless a later effective version was published with "re-plan existing". Past days are never re-planned (the planner and sync already start from today).

**Settings that were already settings** (laundry operations, the two laundry draft fields, reminder switches, recurring jobs, auto-assign, route, auto clock-out, the five QA automation fields) are owned by the rule service. When a version becomes live its values are mirrored into the `app` settings row (`writeSchedulingRuleSettings`, patch in place) so every existing reader keeps reading the same place; the hourly `scheduling-rules-activate` job and every rule read perform the activation. `saveAppSettings` now reads and writes inside one transaction under the advisory lock `AppSetting:app` (shared with the mirror, so neither can overwrite the other from a stale read; a read failure fails the save instead of merging over defaults) and always keeps the stored rule-owned fields: the generic settings PATCH reports attempted changes (`schedulingRulesIgnored`, header `X-Scheduling-Rules-Ignored`) and the whole-blob audit restore leaves the rules untouched. The laundry, safeguards, notification automation, comms control center, classic settings editor and classic notifications page show these fields read-only with a link.

**Screen** (Settings › Operations › Scheduling rules, `/v2/admin/settings/scheduling-rules`; catalog key `scheduling-rules`, `?tab=scheduling-rules` redirects; ops-catalog area Settings). ADMIN and OPS_MANAGER may view (audited `SCHEDULING_RULES_VIEWED`, once per person per 10 minutes). Tabs Laundry, Jobs (with the read-only worker schedule), History and Backups. Loading, unavailable (503 with reason and Retry), stale (last loaded rules kept with a notice) and ready are separate states.

**Locked edit flow** (`service.ts`). Capability `scheduling.rules_edit` (grant tier, ADMIN only until granted) and sensitive action of the same name. Unlock: `requireDelegatedAction` (refused while testing as someone) plus the person's own PIN; a 15-minute unlock bound to that person (`AppSetting scheduling_rules_unlock:<id>`, token hash only). Draft (kept across tabs and on any failure), plain diff, dry run (`preview.ts`: laundry new runs planned differently and existing pending runs that would move, future turnovers re-timed, tonight's recurring count), "Test against last month" (replays the last 30 days, saves nothing). Publish needs the unlock, the PIN again, a reason of 8+ characters, the reviewed checkbox and a second confirmation, an effective day from tomorrow, and the version the review was based on (409 `STALE` otherwise); 10-minute cool-down (429). Default: only new runs and jobs follow the new rules; existing pending ones move only if "Re-plan these N" is ticked (laundry still through its usual review). A pre-change snapshot and the version row and the audit `SCHEDULING_RULES_PUBLISHED` (before, after, changes, reason, snapshot id) are written in one locked transaction.

**History, restore and backups.** Compare any two versions; "Restore this version" goes through the same review and must use exactly that version's values (kind RESTORE). Backups (`backup.ts`): JSON download with every version and a checksum, optionally per-property calendar options, recurring rules and partner schedules (reference only, never written back); stored snapshots before every publish, weekly (`scheduling-rules-weekly-snapshot`, Monday 02:40) and on request; restore from a snapshot or an uploaded file validates format, rules format, checksum and every value, then publishes as kind IMPORT through the same flow. Audit actions: `SCHEDULING_RULES_SEEDED`, `_ACTIVATED`, `_UNLOCKED`, `_PUBLISHED`, `_SNAPSHOT`, `_BACKUP_DOWNLOADED`, `_VIEWED`. System rows use the new `SYSTEM_SCHEDULING_RULES` actor marker.

**Not built / left as is.** Rework offer TTL stays in Accountability. Recurring rule definitions, per-property iCal options and partner schedules keep their own editors (they are per-record data); backups record them but do not restore them. `getAppSettings` still falls back to defaults on a database read error for every other reader (unchanged for unrelated settings); for these rules the planner, iCal job sync and sweeps read the versioned store instead and fail closed. The worker's existing recurring/auto clock-out/reminder handlers still read the mirrored settings through `getAppSettings`.

**People's saves never fail on the rules (follow-up 2026-11-14).** Scheduling work fails closed; a person's own save does not. When a cleaner reports laundry (early update or final submission) and the rules cannot be read, the submission and outcome still commit: no run is created, the outcome is kept in `AppSetting laundry_run_unplanned:<jobId>` with the reason, an audit row `LAUNDRY_RUN_NOT_PLANNED` is written on the job, the job page's Laundry stage reads "Laundry run not planned: scheduling rules could not be read", and the laundry-status response carries `laundryRunNotPlanned`. `ensureLaundryTaskForJob` reads the rules on the main client, never the caller's transaction, so a failed read cannot abort the cleaner's save. The hourly `scheduling-rules-activate` job then runs `retryUnplannedLaundryRuns` (`lib/scheduling-rules/unplanned-laundry-retry.ts`): while the rules are still unreadable it does nothing; once readable it plans the run with the live rules and replays the cleaner's outcome onto it (audit `LAUNDRY_RUN_PLANNED_AFTER_RETRY`, row removed). Other human paths checked: the property key-lost toggle already saves the property and only logs a failed re-plan; manual job creation does not read the rules; Generate week is itself scheduling work and answers with the reason; the plan brief only omits the deadline it would have guessed; iCal runs record ERROR.

**Safeguards QA save (fixed).** `saveAppSettings` now merges `qaAutomation` instead of replacing it, so saving the Safeguards screen (five fields) no longer resets `assignedOnly` and `createIssueTicket` to defaults. Regression: `tests/lib/settings-qa-automation-merge.test.ts`; cleaner path: `tests/db/scheduling-rules-cleaner.test.ts`.

**Tests.** `tests/lib/scheduling-rules-parity.test.ts` (literals, re-exports, defaults vs `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, seed from live settings, registry, 11 planner golden fixtures with exact flag notes, zero UPDATE items on unchanged data, existing runs keep their version, turnover times and priority tables, recurring dry run, auto-pause, driver nudge, clock cutoffs, rule-field preservation, rule book), `tests/lib/scheduling-rules-runtime.test.ts` (fail-closed reads, planner stops, dispatch score 102.25/61.5, day-reminder window), `tests/api/scheduling-rules-routes.test.ts`, `tests/components/scheduling-rules-workspace.test.tsx`, `tests/db/scheduling-rules.test.ts` (seed once from live settings under concurrency, locked publish refusals, concurrent publish, activation and mirroring, generic save blocked, restore, backup round trip and tamper, damaged row).

## AI provider layer: local or cloud per feature, encrypted keys, audit, usage (2026-11-14)

Owner request: "rebuild the AI photo verification and all related to AI… allow to change the model local/cloud… make it easy to connect Hermes or Claude". This wave is step 1 of 4 (provider layer). Steps 2 (photo integrity), 3 (photo verification rebuilt) and 4 (agent identity and read-only connection) follow; assistant features and agent write tools are later work.

**Defaults pending owner confirmation** (set by the lead, recorded for the owner): providers offered are Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, any OpenAI-compatible https endpoint and local Ollama; photos go to a cloud provider only when an administrator allows it per feature (off by default; with it off a photo feature runs only on Ollama or says "AI unavailable for this feature: images are not allowed to leave the server"); every AI result stays a suggestion a person confirms; only administrators change AI settings.

**One layer** (`lib/ai/provider/`). `generateStructured()` (`generate.ts`) is the only way the app asks a model for data. Per call it re-reads the route, then refuses before any request (`AiUnavailableError`, a safe message shown to the person) when the feature is off or not built, a queued job's provider was deselected, the provider is not configured, photos may not leave the server, or the hourly limit is used; otherwise it sends the request through one adapter, validates the answer with the domain zod schema (refinements included) and makes exactly one repair request when the answer is invalid JSON or fails the schema (the repair prompt names field paths, never the answer). Retries: only 429 and 5xx, at most two, honouring Retry-After (capped 10 s), never for local Ollama; timeouts, refusals, 4xx and transport errors are not retried. Adapters: Anthropic through the official SDK with native structured output for text and images (`adapters/anthropic.ts`; this fixes the old social-composer and wording paths that sent no schema and, for the composer, no system prompt), OpenAI Responses (`lib/ai/openai-vision.ts`, now carrying a provider code), OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions with a strict JSON schema (`adapters/openai-compatible.ts`; https only, `assertSafePublicUrl` DNS check on save and on every call, no redirects, 1 MB response cap), and Ollama (`lib/ai/ollama.ts`, unchanged hardening: private address, installed local model, no cloud routing, its own deadline).

**Routing** (`routing-schema.ts`, `routing.ts`; `AppSetting ai_routing_v1`, no migration). Features: `photo_compare`, `photo_assign`, `text_compose`, `wording`, `assistant`, `agent_summaries` (the last two reserved; always unavailable until built). Resolution per request: the feature's own route; else photo features use the photo provider in AI workflow settings (`ai_vision_v1`, unchanged) and text features the saved default route; else the server environment selection (`AI_TEXT_PROVIDER`, Ollama "use for text"). Per feature: on/off, route, "allow photos to go to a cloud provider" (photo features), requests per person per hour (defaults 600/120/30/30/60/60) and the cloud deadline (10–300 s, default 30). Owner-entered model prices (USD per million tokens) drive the cost estimate; a model without a price is "Not known", never $0; Ollama has no provider charge.

**Queued work and deselection.** A photo review stores the `photo_compare` route at queue time (`snapshotRoute` inside its settings snapshot; never saved as a setting). Processing refuses it when the current provider differs ("Photo analysis provider changed. Request a fresh review with the current provider.", now kept as the review's error instead of the generic text). Older snapshots without a route compare their stored provider as before.

**Stamp on photos.** Cleaner evidence (`forms/`, `jobs/` keys) is marked `evidenceStamp` by `loadVisionImage`. Before a cloud request the layer blacks out the bottom band that can hold the burned-in time, date and address (`stamp-mask.ts`): the height follows `lib/uploads/stamp.ts` geometry for four meta lines plus 10%, evaluated at the current width (conservative because photos only shrink after stamping); `tests/lib/ai-stamp-mask.test.ts` pins the constants to stamp.ts, so a stamp change fails the test. Admin reference photos are not masked; Ollama receives photos unchanged. Limits: an unstamped photo loses its bottom band too; house numbers or mail visible in the photo itself are not detected.

**Keys** (`store.ts`, `admin.ts`, `POST /api/admin/ai/credentials`). Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible keys are stored encrypted (`encryptSecret`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY` required; refused with a clear reason when absent) in `AppSetting ai_provider_credentials_v1`. The environment key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY`) applies until a key is saved; Remove saves an explicit "none" (no environment fallback). Saving or removing needs the administrator's password (10 attempts per 15 minutes per person, shared counter), never while testing as someone, and audits `AI_PROVIDER_KEY_CHANGED` with the provider and action only. Reads show the state and the last four characters. A ciphertext that cannot be decrypted (or a plaintext value) fails closed. The general integration-credentials store still keeps its other keys in plain JSON; moving them to encryption is outside this wave.

**Audit and usage.** `AiCall` (migration `20261114040000_ai_provider_layer`): one row per request with feature, provider, model, actor user, agent (reserved for step 4), entity type and id, input/output tokens, image count, attempts, latency, outcome (OK, INVALID_OUTPUT, TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, NOT_CONFIGURED, IMAGES_NOT_ALLOWED, DISABLED, PROVIDER_CHANGED), error code and cost in micro-USD (null when unknown). Never a prompt, answer, image bytes or personal data. A database trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE (append-only). A failed audit write is logged and never blocks the person. `RateLimitWindow` holds atomic fixed-window counters shared by all replicas (also used by step 4). Monthly usage (`usage.ts`) groups the organisation-timezone month by feature, provider and model with succeeded, failed, refused, tokens, known cost and the count of calls whose cost is not known.

**Slow work.** `AiTask` + pg-boss job `ai-tasks` (every minute, leased, two attempts) runs the per-feature connection tests; the screen polls `GET /api/admin/ai/tests/[id]` (requester only) and says when it is still waiting for the worker. Photo comparison keeps its existing `AiPhotoReview` queue (`ai-photo-review`). Photo assignment is still a bounded request while the cleaner waits (unchanged in this wave).

**Screens.** Settings has a new "AI" category (`settings-catalog.ts`): "AI providers and models" (`?tab=ai`, `components/v2/admin/settings/ai-section.tsx`), "Photo checks and memory" (the existing `/v2/admin/ai`, URL kept) and "Ollama" (moved from System). The AI screen: provider cards (key state, last four, save/remove with password; the compatible endpoint's https address and name; Ollama links to its setup), the default text provider, one card per feature (status, current provider and where it comes from, on/off, own provider and model, cloud photo switch, hourly limit, deadline, "Run a real test" with made-up content or generated colour cards, polled), model prices, a sticky Save with a stale-write guard (409 keeps the draft and offers "Put my changes on top" or "Load theirs"), and this month's usage. Saves audit `AI_SETTINGS_UPDATED` with before and after (routing holds no secrets). Administrators only; OPS managers keep read access to the photo workflow page as before.

**Features moved onto the layer, meaning unchanged.** Photo comparison and assignment keep their prompts, schemas, thresholds, the reviewer approval route and every rule in it (the AI never writes `QAReview`); identity checks moved into the schema so a mismatch gets the one repair. Photo assignment now refuses up front, with the safe reason, when photos may not leave the server (409; uploads kept, assign manually), and passes the cleaner as the actor. Notification wording "Regenerate" and the social composer keep their proposals-only behaviour; a refusal (hourly limit, switched off) returns its reason. The compose route reports the `text_compose` route.

**Verification.** See `docs/qa/recent-changes-review-2026-10-09.md`, "AI provider layer (2026-11-14)".

## Laundry run full page, Change state and Void (2026-11-14)

Owner request: "Admin needs to void skipped or flagged laundry schedules and it will be removed from the schedule and invoices. Also admin can mark whether it was already done or not, like change the state of each laundry task. Also each laundry task can be opened and viewed separately as a job does." Boards LaundryRunDetail, LaundryRunActions and LaundryPipelineEntry. Left uncommitted in the working tree. One forward migration: `20261114030000_laundry_run_void`.

**Defaults pending owner confirmation** (the lead's stated defaults, applied as written):
- Change state: ADMIN, and OPS_MANAGER with the Laundry pack at manage (new capability `laundry.change_state`, tier manage).
- Void and Undo void: ADMIN only, the person's own PIN (new sensitive action `laundry.void`; capability `laundry.void` is an administrator capability, tier grant: off for everyone else unless an administrator grants it to a person, like the other administrator capabilities). Refused while testing as someone (`actualActorRefusal`).
- Void is offered on Skipped and Flagged runs and on failed runs still Pending or Confirmed (a failed-pickup row is recorded).
- A run is locked against Void once a laundry report containing it has been emailed (the only "issued" trace that exists); a run on an emailed report cannot move back past Dropped off.
- A voided run also disappears from the laundry partner's own Invoices screen.
- "Create a replacement run" is not built (see below).

**Schema.** `LaundryTask.voidedAt`, `voidedById`, `voidReason`, `voidPreviousStatus` (all nullable) and an index on `voidedAt`. No new `LaundryStatus` value: a voided run is stored as `SKIPPED_PICKUP` (the existing durable soft state that every board leaves out and the planner refuses to touch) and marked with the four columns; a CHECK constraint (`LaundryTask_void_complete_check`) requires who, why, the previous state and `SKIPPED_PICKUP` whenever `voidedAt` is set, so nothing can change the state of a voided run behind the void. Verified with `prisma migrate deploy` on a fresh database (`createdb laundry_void_fresh`) and on the existing `sneek_ui`, repeated (no pending migrations), and `prisma migrate diff --exit-code` reported no difference at the time; later diffs show only other sessions' in-progress models (`AiCall`, `RateLimitWindow`, `AiTask`, `SubmissionMedia.capturedAt`).

**Change state** (`lib/laundry/run-correction-rules.ts` pure rules; `lib/laundry/run-corrections.ts` service; `POST /api/admin/laundry/runs/state`). Choices: Not picked up yet (Confirmed when the cleaner's handoff said ready, else Waiting for pickup), Picked up and at the laundry (one stored state, PICKED_UP), Ready to return, Dropped off, Skipped (skip reason), Flagged (flag note). A later state requires the real date and time it happened (the dialog starts empty; never in the future; never before the cleaner's latest ready handoff; a drop-off never before the pickup; Ready to return and Dropped off also ask the pickup time when none is recorded), who did it (an active laundry team member who works on the run, or an office person) and a reason. Bags, weight and price are optional; blank leaves the stored value as it is and is never written as 0. Moving back is allowed after the warning is confirmed (`acknowledgeBackwards`), and refused past Dropped off when the run is on an emailed report. One transaction locks the run, checks the version shown (`expectedUpdatedAt`, 409 otherwise), updates the run, adds a LaundryConfirmation row (event `OFFICE_CORRECTION` with the before values, the times, who did it and the reason) and an audit row `LAUNDRY_OFFICE_CORRECTION` (actor, effective role, the administrator behind a Test-as session). No earlier confirmation, photo or receipt is edited. Nothing is sent unless "Tell them in their portal inbox" is ticked; then an inbox notice goes to the run's partner team through the notification pipeline (the existing `laundry.team_request` type, `transports: ["INBOX"]`, never email, SMS or push). The laundry team's own pickup or drop-off arriving after a correction already recorded that leg (for example saved on a phone without signal) is kept beside it as its own row (`TEAM_RECORD_AFTER_OFFICE_CORRECTION`, with its photo) and never applied over it (`keepTeamRecordBesideCorrection`, called by the status route). Several runs: one state and one real time for all, each run checked on its own, one outcome per run. Edit no longer has a Status field (it stamped the time of the save); it says to use Change state and no longer sends `status`.

**Void and Undo void** (`POST /api/admin/laundry/runs/void`, `POST /api/admin/laundry/runs/void/undo`). Reason required; own PIN (`verifySensitiveAction(..., "laundry.void")`, 423 on a refused PIN). The run becomes `SKIPPED_PICKUP` with who, when, why and the previous state; it is taken off every draft or active laundry route; a waiting failed-pickup skip or delete request closes as "Voided by office" (row `FAILED_PICKUP_REQUEST_VOIDED`); audit `LAUNDRY_RUN_VOIDED`. Refusals carry the reason: already voided, not voidable, on an emailed report. Several runs: one reason and one PIN, an outcome per run. Undo void restores the previous state, clears the void columns, adds `RUN_VOID_UNDONE` (keeping the void's who, when and why in the row and in audit `LAUNDRY_RUN_VOID_UNDONE`) and reopens the skip request the void closed. Route stops are not put back (the route builder or planner adds them again). Edit, Change state, planned times, bag custody and both delete routes refuse a voided run (409 "undo the void first"); its record is never deleted through them.

**Emailed reports.** `logLaundryReportActivity` now records `taskIds` and `dateField` on every laundry report audit row. `emailedReportContaining` locks a run when an emailed report lists it (or is the one-run report for it); an earlier batch report that did not list its runs locks a run when its range covers one of the run's dates and it was for all properties or the run's property (the cautious answer: a wrong "no" would rewrite an issued record).

**The planner and the cleaner never undo a void.** `buildLaundrySyncDraft` skips voided runs as it skips completed ones; `applyLaundryPlanDraft` refuses them (they are also `SKIPPED_PICKUP`); `applyCleanerLaundryStatusUpdate` returns a voided run unchanged. No rule value and no other planner decision changed; `tests/lib/scheduling-rules-parity.test.ts` passes unchanged.

**LaundryTask query audit** (every read of `LaundryTask`, decided):
- Excluded explicitly (`voidedAt: null`, `lib/laundry/void-scope.ts`): Pipeline day query and Runs today tile (`pipeline-server.ts`); week feed and route-builder current window (`week-feed.ts`, with `includeVoided` for the office's Completed history only); `filterTasksVisibleToUser` and `laundryTaskScope` for laundry accounts (portal Today, Runs, Tracking, route stops, From the office, stop page, attention counts, portal stats, portal invoices); portal history route and v1 laundry calendar; laundry invoice and report data (`invoice.ts`; admin Costs and invoices, partner Invoices, PDFs and emails); finance summary laundry cost and turnover profit; team metrics; statistics (`stats-load.ts`, v1 stats page, portal stats counts); calendar counts (`lib/calendar/load.ts`, `/api/admin/laundry/calendar`); Command glance and daily briefing counts; v1 ops page; live drivers day list (`/api/admin/laundry/live`); supplier directory figures; bag custody list; client portal laundry list, property laundry, home dashboard, client job page and job API (a voided run shows as no laundry run), v1 client page; property preview "last laundry"; client cleaning report (falls back to the cleaner's form answers).
- Already left out because a voided run is `SKIPPED_PICKUP`: lanes (`classifyLane`), exceptions, alerts and Approvals (FLAGGED only), reminders and driver nudge (status lists), cleaner nudges and team requests (`laundryTeamRequestKinds`), Chase supplier (at the laundry only), tomorrow prep and admin attention summary (`notIn DROPPED, SKIPPED`), portfolio facts (open statuses), portal search (`status not SKIPPED_PICKUP`), route candidates overdue, failed pickup (Pending or Confirmed only), reschedule (refuses skipped), partner entries (by status), work queue and immediate attention (FLAGGED).
- Shown as Voided on purpose: the run page, Completed history under the Voided filter, the job page's Laundry stage ("Voided by office", with "Open run").
- Shown as skipped, left as is: admin glance views that show a job's laundry status (job peek, property overview Coming up cell, QA job view, cleaner briefing and form route) show "Skipped / no pickup"; the run page says Voided.
- Writes: planner, cleaner status, status route, admin PATCH, deletes, planned times, bag custody refuse or skip a voided run as above. `lib/ical/sync.ts` and the job delete and reset routes still delete a job's laundry run and its rows when the job itself is removed (unchanged behaviour for every run).

**Run full page** `/v2/admin/laundry/runs/[id]` (`app/v2/admin/laundry/runs/[id]/page.tsx`, loader `lib/laundry/run-page-load.ts`, card facts `loadRunCard`, pure page rules `lib/laundry/run-page-rules.ts`, components `components/v2/admin/laundry/run/*`). Breadcrumb ← Laundry, title "Property · R-xxxxxx" with the state, stage bar (six steps; Picked up and At the laundry drawn as two steps of one stored state; failed pickups mark the step pending) with Flagged, Skipped and Voided beside it, seven key facts ("Not recorded" for anything missing), one primary action by state (voided → Undo void; waiting skip request → Decide skip request; waiting for pickup → Ask laundry team: confirm pickup; at the laundry over turnaround → Chase supplier; at the laundry → when will it be back / drop time; dropped without a photo → Ask laundry team for photo; otherwise Change state, or the run report), Change state beside it, and a More menu (Edit run details, Reschedule, Change state, Download run report, Open in Pipeline side panel, Copy link; Danger zone: Skip or delete, Void this run or Undo void, with the reason when not offered). A needs-you notice, then tabs Timeline, Photos, Requests and replies, History; the timeline is Cleaner handoff → Pickup (failed pickups with who, reason, outcome and photo; requests; planned times; the skip decision) → At the laundry (weight, price, team answers, Chase supplier) → Ready to return → Drop-off → Invoice (on an emailed report, not yet, or none for a voided run, with the honest note that today's report prints $0.00 for a missing price). Office corrections are listed above the timeline. Right rail: Laundry partner and team, Property and access, Linked job (next clean and next guest), Money, Exceptions, History (All / Office corrections / Voided). Times in the organisation's time zone; calendar days unshifted. Phone: the header buttons move to `EPhoneActionBar`, `ESectionSwitcher` jumps between the timeline and rail cards, dialogs are bottom sheets. Every side panel function has a home: status and exceptions (header, notice, Exceptions), clean link (Linked job, handoff), pickup and drop (facts, stages), next guest (Linked job), partner, team and route (Partner card), client (Property card), bags, weight, cost (facts, At the laundry, Money), team answers (At the laundry, Requests tab), planned times (Pickup stage), flag, skip and override notes (Exceptions), address, buffer and key lost (Property card), history (History card and tab), evidence (Photos tab), replace evidence (Photos tab), requests and Chase supplier (stages, Requests tab, primary), Edit, Reschedule, Task report (More), Open linked job (Linked job), Skip or delete (Danger zone). The side panel stays and gains "Open full page".

**Links.** Pipeline cards: "Open run" and a ⋯ menu (Open run, Open side panel, Edit, Move to another day, Change state, Skip or delete, and Void run on voidable runs for those who may void). Bulk bar: Move to, Change state, Void selected, with a result list per run. A "Voided N" chip (runs voided in the last 30 days) opens Completed history on the new Voided filter, where voided runs are struck through with the reason. Calendar: a day with one laundry run opens that run's page. Job page Laundry stage: "Open run". Laundry portal stop page: office accounts see "Open the office run page". Phone Pipeline (board M-LaundryStock): the four lanes become a segmented control with counts, and exceptions in the other lanes show as one note.

**Not built.** "Create a replacement run": `LaundryTask.jobId` is required and unique and most laundry code reads the run's job, so a run without a job is too invasive for this change; the Void dialog says so and asks the office to plan linen for the next clean. No adjustment line on laundry reports (there is no stored laundry invoice).

**Tests.** `tests/lib/laundry-run-corrections.test.ts` (real time required, future and before-handoff refused, pickup asked when missing, drop not before pickup, reason, same state, skip and flag fields, Not picked up yet target, backwards warning, emailed-report block, figures never zero, void rights by state, refusals with reasons, undo, emailed report lock incl. legacy reports, the status → primary action table, stage bar, off-track, skip request closed and reopened). `tests/components/laundry-run-actions.test.tsx` (time starts empty, save blocked until time, who and reason, the version and null figures sent, a refused save keeps the answers, backwards confirmation, bulk outcomes). `tests/db/laundry-run-void.test.ts` (PostgreSQL: stale and missing time refused, correction recorded with originals byte-equal and audited with role, nothing sent, the team's later record kept beside; void refused for an operations manager, a wrong PIN, a non-voidable run and an emailed report; bulk outcomes; who, when, why and the closed request; exclusion from Pipeline, feeds, portal scope and reports; planner and cleaner never change it; edits refused; Undo void restores and reopens; the CHECK constraint). `tests/api/client-laundry-filters.test.ts` expectations now include `voidedAt: null`.

## Photo integrity checks: duplicates, reuse from earlier cleans, camera time (2026-11-14)

Step 2 of the AI rebuild. Deterministic facts, no AI, shown as flags for a person; never a verdict, never a score, never shown to clients or cleaners.

**Facts** (`lib/media/photo-integrity.ts`; migration `20261114050000_photo_integrity`, nullable columns on `SubmissionMedia`): `contentSha256` (exact bytes), `perceptualHash` (64-bit difference hash of the picture with the stamp areas cropped: the bottom time/address band from the stamp geometry and a top strip for the tag and logo, so the same picture stamped again at another time still matches), `capturedAt` and `capturedAtSource` (EXIF DateTimeOriginal with its OffsetTimeOriginal = "exif-offset"; without an offset it is read in the business time zone = "exif-local"), `integrityCheckedAt` and `integrityError` (fixed text). Null means "Not checked" or "Not recorded", never a pass.

**When** (`lib/media/photo-integrity-queue.ts`, pg-boss `media-integrity` every 5 minutes, 40 photos per run, newest first). Uploads go straight to storage, so the server reads the stored bytes after submission rather than at upload; existing photos are filled the same way from their stored bytes (honest to compute). A photo that cannot be read, or lives outside `forms/` or `jobs/`, is marked checked with a reason and shown as "Could not check". Capture time comes from the stored photo or, when it has none and an original upload was kept, from the original.

**Limit, stated on screen:** the in-app stamp re-saves photos without camera data, so most stamped evidence has no capture time and the clock comparison covers only photos that kept EXIF. Reading the camera time on the device before stamping is follow-up work.

**Flags** (`lib/media/photo-integrity-flags.ts`, `GET /api/qa/jobs/[id]/photo-integrity`): the same file used twice in the job; a near-identical picture in the job (2 or fewer of 64 bits differ); the same file or a near-identical picture (2 bits or fewer) submitted for an earlier clean at the same property (last 3,000 photos there); a camera time more than 30 minutes outside the job's clock times (first clock-in to last clock-out, or now while clocked in). The thresholds are strict because cleaners photograph the same spots every clean; a flag names the earlier clean's date and asks the person to check. Access: ADMIN and OPS_MANAGER, and a QA inspector only on an assigned job (inspectors get no link to the other job). Shown as a lazy "Photo checks" disclosure at the foot of the AI photo review panel, so it appears on the QA job page and the admin job's submission stage without loading until opened, and resets when the job changes; times are formatted in the business time zone.

## AI photo verification rebuilt: per-field checks, cannot tell, regions, points, agreement, opt-out (2026-11-14)

Step 3 of the AI rebuild. No schema change (settings live in `ai_vision_v1` and a new AppSetting).

**Per-field checks** (`checkFieldPhotos` in `lib/ai/vision.ts`, queue in `lib/ai/photo-review.ts`). The background review now sends one request per checklist field (photos chunked at 8, or 1 for local Ollama; at most 4 reference photos) with the field's reference photos and its optional acceptance criteria. Every submitted photo gets an outcome: **meets**, **issue** (each finding names the criterion, what was observed, the reference it differs from and, when it can be located, a normalised region of the submitted photo) or **cannot tell** (first-class, always with a reason: not in frame, blurred, dark, blocked, angle). A field with neither a reference photo nor criteria is **not checked** without any request. The schema refuses unknown photos or references, issue without findings, findings without issue, cannot tell without a reason and regions outside the photo; a mismatch gets the layer's single repair request. The model states a confidence band (low/medium/high); it is stored with the number used for the unchanged eligibility rule (0.4/0.7/0.9 against the minimum confidence, default 0.8, so only high-confidence findings are deductible by default). Stored results keep the older per-photo shape plus the new fields, so older reviews still display.

**Acceptance criteria** (form builder, question settings, Example media: "AI photo check: acceptance criteria (optional)", `FormField.aiCriteria`, up to 1,000 characters). Office only, never shown to cleaners; sent to the model as data written by the office, not instructions. Adding criteria changes the form revision fingerprint like any schema edit.

**Suggestions only; approval unchanged.** The reviewer approval route keeps every rule (human selection, reason, expected review and score, one photo deduction per QA review, no double deduction over an existing QA issue, invoiced jobs refused, impersonation refused, transaction and audit). The AI never writes `QAReview`. Deduction points are now settings (`minorPoints` default 2, `majorPoints` default 5; a minor finding cannot exceed a major one; Settings, AI workflow page) read from the review's own snapshot, so a review keeps the points it was queued with; with the defaults the result is identical to the old rule (500-case parity test). Saving photo check settings is now audited (`AI_VISION_SETTINGS_UPDATED`) and refused while testing as someone.

**Review panel** (`components/v2/qa/photo-review-panel.tsx`): outcome per photo (Meets the standard (suggestion), Review suggested issue, Cannot tell, Not checked), the cannot-tell reason, the criteria, the confidence band, numbered boxes on the submitted photo for located findings, and the deduction preview with the review's points. While analysis runs it re-reads quietly every 5 seconds instead of asking the person to refresh.

**Agreement with inspectors** (`lib/ai/photo-review-evaluation.ts`, AI workflow page): evaluation labels come from every stored reviewer decision: a finding selected in an approved deduction is confirmed, one left out is not selected, findings in dismissed suggestions are dismissed. Per provider and model over 90 days: reviews, findings by label, agreement (confirmed / labelled; "No labelled findings" rather than a default percentage) and photos with cannot tell / not checked. It does not measure issues the AI missed (no label exists for those).

**Per-property opt-out** (`lib/ai/photo-review-opt-out.ts`, `GET|PUT /api/admin/ai/photo-review-opt-out`, panel on the AI workflow page). Opted-out properties are never queued; a queued review for one stops with "This property is opted out of AI photo review."; Analyze is refused with the same reason. Saves are revisioned (409 with the current list) and audited (`AI_PHOTO_REVIEW_OPT_OUT_UPDATED`); an unreadable list pauses AI photo review for every property and never blocks a cleaner's submission. Photo integrity checks (no AI) still run.

## Agent connection (Hermes, Claude): read-only MCP server, agent tokens, Settings › Access › Agents (2026-11-14)

Step 4 of the AI rebuild. Agents can **read** operations within the access an administrator gives them. Step 6 added write tools that only **ask**: see "Agent actions: requests that wait for a person's approval" below. Migration `20261114060000_agent_connection`.

**Defaults pending owner confirmation:** only ADMIN creates, rotates or revokes agents and pauses them all, each time with their own PIN (`verifySensitiveAction`), never while testing as someone, audited; an agent never exceeds its creator's access and never gets administrator rights, PINs, passwords, credentials or keys; tokens are shown once, stored only as a hash, expire (1 to 365 days, default 90) and are revocable at once; reads need no approval; messaging clients or guests will always need a person's approval (step 6); OAuth for the Claude apps connector comes later.

**Identity** (`AgentProfile`, `AgentToken`; `lib/agents/access.ts`). Deliberate change from the design: an agent is **not** a `User` row, so it can never sign in, never appears in people lists or role queries and has no password field at all. `AgentProfile` holds name, creator, scope packs and status (ACTIVE / REVOKED). `AgentToken` holds the sha-256 hash, a short prefix for recognition, expiry, last use (updated at most once a minute) and revocation; rotating revokes every live token of the agent in the same transaction. Tokens are `snk_agent_` plus 256 random bits.

**Access, recomputed on every request.** Scope packs (`lib/agents/scopes.ts`, read-only): Jobs, Laundry, Cases, Approvals, Stock, Properties, Staff lookup, Client lookup, Invoices (also needs `invoices.view`), Pay requests; each maps to an existing office area. Effective access = the agent's packs ∩ what its creator can read **now** (`readableScopesFor`: an active ADMIN reads every pack; an active OPS_MANAGER only areas at read or above in the live policy, and the capability where needed; anyone else or a deactivated or deleted account: nothing). A creator who loses an area takes it away from the agent on its next call ("withheld" on screen and in `whoami`); a creator with no access left blocks the agent (403). Creating an agent with a pack wider than the creator's access is refused.

**Authentication** (`authenticateAgent`). Bearer token only, looked up by hash; refused when unknown, revoked, expired, the agent is revoked, all agents are paused (`AppSetting agents_paused_v1`), or the creator has no access; then shared limits per token through `RateLimitWindow` (60 requests a minute, 5,000 a day; 429 with Retry-After). No cookies are read and nothing calls the app over HTTP. Agent tokens are accepted **only** by `/api/agent/mcp`; session routes never read an Authorization header (`lib/auth/session.ts` is unchanged).

**MCP server** (`POST /api/agent/mcp`, `lib/agents/mcp.ts`). Implemented directly rather than with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (not a dependency; the surface is small and this avoids a new package and transport adapter under Next 14 route handlers): JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP with JSON responses, stateless (no session id, no SSE stream; GET and DELETE answer 405), batches refused. Methods: `initialize` (protocol 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 or 2024-11-05), `notifications/initialized` (202), `ping`, `tools/list` (only the tools the agent may use now, all annotated read-only), `tools/call`. A tool outside the agent's access returns a tool error; bad arguments are refused with the field names.

**Tools** (`lib/agents/tools.ts`): `whoami`; `list_today_jobs` (a date within 14 days); `get_job` (id or job number; property without access details; laundry and open cases only if those packs are held); `live_ops_summary` (today's jobs by status, jobs without a cleaner, flagged laundry and open cases when allowed); `laundry_runs`; `list_cases`; `approvals_waiting` (pay requests and QA outcomes only, labelled partial); `stock_needs`; `find_properties`; `find_people` (staff or clients, each needing its own pack); `invoice_summary` (25 latest invoices and counts by status; no sums are calculated); `pay_summary` (25 oldest pay requests waiting). Every query names its fields, so access codes, alarm codes, key locations, access guides, internal notes, phone numbers, bank details, password and two-step secrets, token hashes and photo keys or bytes are never returned (a test scans both the queries and every tool's output). Missing values read "not recorded", never zero. Text written by clients, guests or cleaners (job notes, case titles, laundry flag notes, stock notes, pay request titles) is returned as `{"untrusted": true, "source": …, "text": …}` with a notice to treat it as data, never instructions; the server's `initialize` instructions say the same. The tools read the database directly with explicit field lists (and `listQaOutcomeApprovals` for QA outcomes) rather than the office screens' loaders, because those return wide records that include access details.

**Audit.** `AgentAuditEntry` (append-only: a database trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE): one row per request, including refused authentication, with agent, token, creator, method, tool, an argument summary limited to each tool's known argument names (strings cut at 80 characters, other values omitted), outcome (OK, REFUSED, DENIED, INVALID, ERROR), error code, result size and latency; never the token. Administrator actions write `AuditLog` rows: AGENT_CREATED, AGENT_TOKEN_ROTATED, AGENT_REVOKED, AGENTS_PAUSED, AGENTS_RESUMED (token prefix and expiry only).

**Screen** (`/v2/admin/settings/agents`, settings catalog "Agents (Hermes, Claude)" under Access, ADMIN only; `components/v2/admin/settings/agents/agents-workspace.tsx`). One h1 from the page header. Pause or resume all agents; New agent (name, read packs limited to the administrator's own access, expiry); every change asks for the administrator's own PIN in place (the prompt keeps the draft and clears only the PIN on refusal); the token appears once with Copy token and Copy MCP configuration, then "I have stored it" removes it; each agent card shows effective and withheld packs, token prefix, expiry, last use, creator, Rotate token, Revoke and a "Recent calls" disclosure (last 10). Cards and lists only, so it works at 390px; tone bands mark withheld access, an expired or missing token.

**How to connect Hermes or Claude.**
1. Settings › Access › Agents › New agent: name it (for example "Hermes"), tick what it may read, choose an expiry, confirm with your PIN.
2. Copy the token shown (only once) into the agent's settings, never into chat or email.
3. Hermes, or any MCP client with a JSON configuration: add an HTTP MCP server with the address shown on the screen (`https://<your app address>/api/agent/mcp`) and the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, for example `{"mcpServers":{"sneek":{"type":"http","url":"https://<your app address>/api/agent/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer <token>"}}}}` (the screen's Copy MCP configuration fills in the real address and token).
4. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http sneek https://<your app address>/api/agent/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`.
5. Claude apps (custom connector): **not available**. The connector needs an OAuth sign-in, which is not built (it was left out of step 6 on purpose).
6. Ask the agent to call `whoami`; the call appears under Recent calls. To stop an agent at once, Revoke it; to stop all, Pause all agents.

**Not built:** the instruction text an agent was given (the protocol carries none), an IP allowlist per token, OAuth for the Claude apps connector. Write tools and `AgentActionRequest` were built in step 6 (next section).

**Risks and mitigations.** Prompt injection through client, guest, cleaner or email text: such fields are marked untrusted in every result and the tools cannot change anything. Token leakage: hash-only storage, shown once, expiry, immediate revoke and rotate, last-used display, per-token limits, the global pause. Over-broad access: read-only packs capped at the creator's live access. Data leaving to the agent's AI provider: whatever an agent reads goes to the provider that runs it; give packs sparingly (finance and people lookups are separate packs).

## Agent actions: requests that wait for a person's approval (2026-11-14)

Step 6 of the AI rebuild. An agent can now **ask** for a small set of changes; it can never make one. Every write tool only creates a request that waits in **Approvals › Agent requests**; approving runs the existing domain service as the approving person. Migration `20261114070000_agent_action_requests`.

**Defaults pending owner confirmation:** write packs are off for every agent until an administrator ticks them (with their own PIN); a request waits 24 hours, then expires; approvers are ADMIN, or OPS_MANAGER with Approvals at Manage **and** the action's own areas at Manage (they decide only what they could do themselves; reject needs the same right); approval is refused while testing as someone; "Pause all agents" stops new requests and stops approvals (reject still works); the waiting notice is inbox only; agent requests are not added to the Approvals badge or the fifteen queue counts.

**Tools** (`lib/agents/action-catalog.ts`, MCP names): `request_reschedule_job` (job id, new date, optional start time, reason; the Calendar move check `checkCalendarMove` is the dry run; approval runs `applyReschedule` with the preview's job version, so the usual cleaner and client schedule notices follow exactly as when a person reschedules, and the preview says so); `request_case_note` (internal, office-only note through `addCaseComment`, office told by `notifyCaseUpdated` with the client never notified); `request_create_case` (operations, lost property or other; never DAMAGE, which raises a repair and tells the client, never a client dispute; never visible to the client; links checked by `validateCaseLinks`; `createCase` with source `AGENT`, the description kept as an internal note; `notifyCaseCreated`); `request_acknowledge_stock_need` (dry run: `validateUrgentStockTransition` from REPORTED; approval: `actOnUrgentStock` with the preview's need version and a stable receipt id; places no order, proves no delivery); `get_action_request` (an agent's own request: status, summary, outcome; offered to agents that have, or had, a write pack). Each write tool needs an `idempotencyKey` (8 to 100 characters, unique per agent): the same key with the same arguments returns the same request, with other arguments it is refused. A refused dry run creates no request and tells the agent why. Tools list them as not read-only and idempotent.

**Left out, with the reason** (no safe domain service to execute through; not reimplemented): assign or reassign a cleaner (the rules — draft, skipped clean, leave conflicts, keeping accepted teammates, the cleaner offer notices and the client introduction — live inside `app/api/admin/jobs/[id]/assign/route.ts`; the only service, `applyAutoAssignment`, skips those guards and notices); an internal note on a job (the job's "Internal note" is one replaceable field inside the serialised job meta, read to the assigned cleaners and written only by the job edit route, which emails and texts cleaners on change); drafting a client message (a client message exists only once sent; drafts live in the browser composer, so storing one would need a new draft store and send path). Never available in any form: invoices, pay, refunds, voids, permissions, users, settings, scheduling rules, deletions, anything sent outside the app.

**Write packs** (`lib/agents/write-scopes.ts`, `AgentProfile.writeAreas`, separate from read packs, default none): "Ask to reschedule jobs" (Jobs and Calendar at Manage), "Ask to open cases and add internal notes" (Cases at Manage), "Ask to acknowledge stock needs" (Inventory at Manage and "Act on urgent stock"). Capped at the creator's **live** Manage access (`manageableWriteScopesFor`; ADMIN every pack), re-checked on every agent call (withheld packs show on the agent card and in `whoami`). Settings › Access › Agents shows what each agent may ask for, its waiting requests, and "Change what it may ask" (own PIN, audited `AGENT_WRITE_AREAS_CHANGED`); New agent has the same tick boxes.

**Requests** (`AgentActionRequest`: agent, token, creator, tool, area, validated arguments, preview, idempotency key, status WAITING / APPROVED / REJECTED / EXPIRED / EXECUTED / FAILED, decided by and at, reason, executed at, result, error, expiresAt default now + 24 h). A database trigger refuses DELETE, any change to what was asked (agent, token, tool, arguments, preview, key) and any status move other than WAITING → APPROVED / REJECTED / EXPIRED / FAILED and APPROVED → EXECUTED / FAILED; a final status never changes. `AgentActionEvent` is the append-only history (trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE, like `AgentAuditEntry`): CREATED (actor none, the agent), APPROVED, REJECTED, EXECUTED, FAILED (the actual person), EXPIRED (none). APPROVED alone means "approved, outcome not recorded" and is never shown as done. Every decision and outcome also writes `AuditLog` (`AGENT_REQUEST_APPROVED`, `_REJECTED`, `_EXECUTED`, `_FAILED`) under the approving person.

**Approval** (`lib/agents/action-execute.ts`, only imported by the approval route; a test walks the MCP server's imports and finds no path to it). In order: the approver is re-read live and must not be testing as someone; the request must still wait and be unexpired (an expired one is marked EXPIRED); the pause must be off; the approver must be able to do the action now; the approver's own PIN where the same action by a person needs one (none of the four does today; the mechanism is per action); the agent must still be active and hold the write pack (otherwise FAILED with the reason); the status moves WAITING → APPROVED with compare-and-set (two approvers cannot both run it); the dry run runs again and the entity state it was made against (job version, case `updatedAt` and state, need version and stage, case links) must be unchanged, otherwise FAILED "… changed after the agent asked … Nothing was applied"; then the service runs as the approver, and the outcome is EXECUTED or FAILED with the service's own message. Fingerprints and idempotent arguments compare with sorted keys because PostgreSQL JSONB reorders them.

**Approvals › Agent requests** (`?tab=agents`, `components/v2/admin/approvals/agent-requests-tab.tsx`; routes `GET /api/admin/agent-requests`, `POST /api/admin/agent-requests/[id]` `{ decision, reason?, credentials? }`, ops-catalog section `agent-requests` → Approvals). Waiting requests oldest first as cards with a honey band: agent and action, the exact change in one sentence, the details and what approving also does, age, asked and expiry times in the organisation timezone; Approve (confirmation, the server's checks named) and Reject (optional reason, kept if the decision is refused); a person who could not decide sees why and the buttons are disabled. Decided requests below with status, outcome and reason (FAILED in wine). Loading, failure, empty and stale are separate; a paused service is said plainly. Phones: stacked cards, full-width decision buttons, the shared section chips for Waiting and Decided, and the shared bottom-sheet dialog.

**Notice** (`lib/notifications/agent-requests.ts`, catalog `agent.action_request`, wording "Request waiting", editable): inbox only through the intent pipeline, event id per request, scope `AGENT_ACTION_APPROVER` (re-checked at queue and dispatch: ADMIN, or OPS_MANAGER with Approvals at least read and the pack's areas at Manage, while the request still waits). The agent's reply says how many inbox notices were taken; queued is not delivered.

**Expiry and pause.** Worker job `agent-request-expiry` (hourly at :10) marks WAITING requests past their time EXPIRED with an event; approval of a lapsed one marks it too; the Approvals list and `get_action_request` already show a lapsed request as expired. `agents_paused_v1` now also refuses request creation (re-read inside the tool after authentication) and approval.

**Not built:** OAuth for the Claude apps connector (not available), the three left-out actions above, agent requests in the Approvals badge, a per-request notice when it expires or is decided (the agent polls).

## Assistant in the app: Ask on Command, Explain this flag, drafts (2026-11-14)

Step 5 of the AI rebuild. Everything runs through the provider layer (Settings, AI) with its own feature, hourly limit and `AiCall` audit: `assistant` (Ask), `explain_flag`, `draft_reply`. All three are text only, so they work with photos-to-cloud off. An older saved routing row without the new features reads with their defaults (on, 60 / 30 an hour). Every feature runs as the signed-in person and is refused while testing as someone; AI off or unconfigured shows a separate "unavailable" state (HTTP 200), never an error.

**Ask** (`lib/assistant/ask.ts`, `POST /api/admin/assistant/ask`, ADMIN and OPS_MANAGER; `components/v2/admin/command/ask-panel.tsx`, a lazy disclosure below the Command heading, one column on phones). Two requests: the model first chooses at most four of the agent read tools (`lib/agents/tools.ts`) offered for the person's **live** access (`readableScopesFor`, the same check that caps agents); the server validates the arguments (unreadable arguments are invalid, never "none") and runs the tools itself; a second request answers only from those results, says when they do not answer the question, and cites records by type and id. Citations are kept only when a tool returned that record, and become links to the job, laundry run, case, property or invoice page. Client and cleaner text stays marked untrusted and the panel says when the answer drew on it. No free-form queries, no writes.

**Explain this flag** (`POST /api/qa/jobs/[id]/photo-review/explain`, same access as photo review: ADMIN, OPS_MANAGER, inspectors on assigned jobs). Buttons beside each AI photo finding, each "cannot tell" result and each photo check flag. The explanation uses only the stored facts (field, criterion, observation, severity, confidence band, whether it is deductible by default, located or compared, the flag's detail); no photo and no storage key is sent.

**Drafts** (`POST /api/admin/assistant/draft`). "Draft with AI" in the message composer when the recipient is a client (an optional note on what to say; reads the client's last six messages, the client's words as untrusted data; told not to promise refunds, discounts, dates or times unless the note says so) and under a saved quote's office notes (reads the quote's facts; told not to change prices). Client replies need `messages.read`; quote notes need the Quotes area. The draft is shown first and only goes into the editor when the person chooses "Use this draft"; sending and saving stay the existing actions with their existing rules.

## Airbnb turnover v3 form (draft for owner review, 2026-11-13)

A new cleaner form written in the form engine's existing format; no engine, builder, cleaner-workspace or schema change. Owner guide (sections, loophole → evidence table, time estimate, import/publish steps, recommended engine additions): `docs/forms/airbnb-turnover-v3.md`.

- **File.** `docs/forms/airbnb-turnover-v3.json`, the Forms library export format (`sneek.form-templates` v1), one form "Airbnb turnover v3", service type `AIRBNB_TURNOVER`, tags v3 / Airbnb / Needs review. 14 sections, 111 questions; `standardSections: false` with its own `arrival-evidence` and `sign-off` sections and a `reported-exceptions` field, so normalizeFormSchema injects nothing. Bedroom and bathroom sections use `repeatBy`; balcony and supplies use the property facts `hasBalcony` / `inventoryEnabled`; the laundry note uses `laundryEnabled`; sofa beds use `sofaBedCount` = 1 or 2 (property rules are equality only). Pool/spa is gated on the cleaner's own answer because there is no property fact for it.
- **Existing flows, not duplicated.** Arrival damage is a Yes / No with the `damage-report` effect; guest items, extra time, leaks, guest-still-present and low dishwasher tablets are instructions pointing to the quick actions (Lost item found, Extra pay request, Maintenance issue, Pause or continue tomorrow, Urgent stock). Nine `stock_count` questions carry `urgent-stock-below`. Laundry bag count, photo and location stay in Wrap up → Laundry handoff (the form only says so). The injected laundry-area and device-charging sections are left to their read-time rules.
- **Stock items.** The file names each counted item by SKU (`DEF-TP` …) because item ids differ per database. `lib/forms/stock-item-binding.ts` (pure) swaps a SKU for the matching active item's id and name, keeps known ids, and reports a missing SKU instead of guessing. Imported through the app as it is, a SKU question counts an unknown item: the count goes to office review and the urgent need is skipped with its reason.
- **Creating the draft.** Forms → Import, or `scripts/seed/airbnb-turnover-v3.ts` (dry run by default, `--apply`, `--actor=`, `--allow-missing-stock`) through `lib/forms/form-file-seed.ts`. The seed binds SKUs, skips a form whose name already exists (idempotent; no "(imported)" copies), then runs the library's own `importFormTemplates`: a new CUSTOM row with `isActive: false`, never published, no other form or job resolution changed. The owner publishes from the builder, which archives the previous global Airbnb form as publishing always does.
- **Engine limits recorded, not built.** No camera-only capture, no video clip count or length, rotation is a fixed per-property cycle rather than random, no pool/pets/BBQ property facts, no numeric property comparisons, no per-bed repeat, no per-property example photos or stock thresholds, no variants, and no AI checks on video.
- **Tests.** `tests/lib/airbnb-turnover-v3-template.test.ts` (18), `tests/db/airbnb-turnover-v3-import.test.ts` (3, disposable PostgreSQL on 55439).

Owner request (testing production on a phone): "Fix all the backends now, redo the small UIs missed." A production build (`.next-audit`) was crawled at 390px for all seven roles (admin, ops, cleaner, client, laundry, QA, maintenance: every static page under `app/v2/<portal>` plus the main record pages), recording every own-API response ≥400, failed or >15s pending request, console/page error and visible error state; admin primary dialogs were opened; safe writes were run on fixtures (case + note, job reschedule and back, laundry run state change and back, stock need report, draft quote). No schema change, no new route or permission.

- **Backend findings.** No 5xx and no ADMIN 403 on its own pages; OPS_MANAGER 403s match its packs (activity, holiday rates, agents, access, test-as, cleaner addresses, diagnostics and the form builder redirect to access denied). The only refusals were correct server answers that the UI asked for anyway: an inspector opening a pool job (`/api/qa/jobs/[id]/progress` and `/photo-review` require an owned assignment) and a client opening another owner's shopping run (404). Diagnostics' `pg_stat_statements` read fails on databases without the extension and is already shown as "not enabled". Write flows all succeeded.

The monitor no longer turns a refused or failed `/progress` read into "No cleaner clocked in yet / Unknown": it says why (`monitorUnavailableText`), stops polling after a 403 and resets per job. The property name wraps on phones.

- **Left lines.** `statusBlockStyle` (classic pages only) set a coloured `borderInlineStart`, which escaped the left-line scan; v2 uses the new `statusTintStyle` (tint only) on cleaner job cards, admin job board cards, laundry queue/history, client laundry and client jobs; `JobStatusProgress` takes `tintOnly`. `tests/lib/no-left-accent-lines.test.ts` now also catches `borderInlineStart`, `statusBlockStyle(` and an untinted `JobStatusProgress` in v2.
- **Phone defects fixed.** `EToneCard` pills are capped at 55% and wrap (Scheduling rules "Eligible cleans" title rendered one letter per line); `EStageBar` is a three-column grid below 640px (laundry run, job and quote stages squeezed "Confirmed" out of its cell); `EStatCard` labels use a smaller, tighter phone eyebrow (mid-word breaks like "CANDIDATE S", "OUTSTANDI NG"); `ETableShell` gains opt-in `phoneStack` (blog posts); client inventory stacks per item on phones; client job progress moved under the heading (compact bar on phones, the seven-column timeline stays from 640px); shopping run pages: one h1 (also in the not-found state), client charges below the run heading, readable enums; hiring role rows no longer squeeze the title; compliance actions wrap (they overflowed left) and "Clear" is no longer red; laundry live-route controls wrap; client reports filter labels no longer overlap; urgent-needs writes refresh the server-rendered "Urgent needs N" tab count; maintenance "By day" no longer calls a past day of finished tickets overdue; client laundry update times use the Sydney zone (hydration mismatch); the laundry run header no longer offers Change state twice when it is the primary action; blog titles wrap on phones; a few phone tap targets enlarged.
- **Left for owners/other agents.** Admin Maintenance page problems are listed in the review record (not restyled; a designer owns it). Forms statistics "Start rejecting…" button overflows its card at 390px (forms library, out of scope). Opening `/v2/admin/onboarding/new` creates a blank draft survey on every visit (inherited from v1; product decision). The cleaner job page PATCHes an empty draft on open of an offered job.

## AI configuration page rebuilt: one page, status strip, five sections, phone layout (2026-11-15)

Owner request: "Redo the AI configuration page, give me a design", boards AiConfiguration, AiConfigurationStates and M-AiConfiguration approved with "use your defaults and build all designs". A page rebuild over the existing APIs; provider behaviour, routing semantics, limits, the AiCall audit and every AI feature's logic are unchanged. No schema change.

**Defaults pending owner confirmation:** (1) operations managers read the page (with the existing "AI tools" ops pack at View or above) and change nothing; administrators acting as themselves make every change (server-enforced, as before); key last-four characters are never sent to non-administrators. (2) No monthly spending cap. (3) One "photos may leave the server" switch per photo feature, as before. (4) Adding, replacing and removing a key is confirmed with the person's own PIN (their password while they have no PIN) through the shared sensitive confirmation; the dialog sends `security: { pin } | { password }` like the other tier C routes; the credential route's verification belongs to another workstream. (5) No automatic fallback to local Ollama when a cloud provider fails: the failure is shown and people continue manually.

**One page** (`/v2/admin/ai`, `app/v2/admin/ai/page.tsx` → `components/v2/admin/ai/`). One h1 ("AI"), no extra main. Old links: `/v2/admin/settings?tab=ai` redirects to it; `?tab=ollama` redirects to `/v2/admin/ai?section=ollama` (opens the Local Ollama setup); the settings catalog keeps `ai` (now `href /v2/admin/ai`, not admin-only), `ai-workflows` (`#photo-checks`) and `ollama` (admin only) in the "Automation and AI" category; the admin nav "AI configuration" entry is unchanged. `SETTINGS_TABS.ai = "ai"` maps the old tab to the AI tools pack.

**Layout.** Status strip (AI on/off/not set up, providers connected and failing, whether photos may leave, this month's cost with requests at an unknown price). 1 Where AI runs: a card per provider with a tone band (sage Connected only after a passed test, wine Failing on a failed test, newer failed real requests or an unreadable key, sky Not set up / Not tested), a Local or Cloud tag naming where requests go, the key's last four, models, last test, used by and this month; Test connection runs the feature test of a feature that uses the provider (text first) and is off while edits are unsaved; Add / Replace / Remove key; the compatible endpoint's address and name; "Ollama setup" opens the existing Ollama tool in place; default for text features and a cloud deadline that sets every feature (a feature's Settings can differ). A failing card says what failed, when, how many real requests failed since the last success, what people see, the likely fix, "Move … to default" and the technical detail. 2 What AI does: one row per feature (on, runs on with "Use default · …", photo switch with its consequence, hourly limit, last test, this month); Agent summaries "Not available yet"; a blocked photo feature (cloud route, photo switch off) gets a honey card with "Use Local Ollama" and "Allow photos to go to …" (a confirmation; it takes effect on save and is in the settings audit; no PIN, see below); a reached hourly limit lists who and when it resets. Settings (desktop) and the phone sheet hold the per-feature deadline, the photo workflow switch (`comparisonEnabled` / `assignmentEnabled`), the photo default provider and model and "Check provider and saved model". 3 Photo checks: confidence bands (lowest band that may propose a deduction maps onto the unchanged minimum confidence; the exact number stays editable), an example finding, points and batches, photo memory and the dedicated recognition service, opted-out properties (Manage dialog, revisioned save), agreement with inspectors, the property photo memory panel in a disclosure. 4 Usage and cost by feature and model with a total; a model without a price is "Not known" with "Add a price", never $0; model prices. 5 Privacy and safety. First run (no provider set up): the 3-step guide replaces Sections 1 to 4 ("Show every setting anyway" keeps them reachable).

**Saving.** One Save changes writes the routing (stale-write guard; a 409 now also names who saved first from the settings audit, and offers Load theirs / Put mine on top) and the photo workflow settings; fields freeze while saving; a failed part keeps its draft. Reads are cancelled when replaced and checked after parsing; loading, failed (retry) and empty are separate; unreadable facts say "Not known".

**API additions** (computed from existing tables, never estimated): `GET /api/admin/ai/settings` is readable by OPS_MANAGER (`requireAiReader`; pack enforced by the existing ops path check), hides key hints from non-administrators and returns `canEdit`, `isAdmin` and `status` (`lib/ai/provider/status.ts`): the latest test per feature with the failed request's error code from AiCall, provider health (last success, last failure, failures since), people who reached an hourly limit in the current window with their count (AiCall RATE_LIMITED + RateLimitWindow), the last AI settings save (AuditLog) and the Ollama host and models. Each part is null when unreadable.

**Phone (below 640px).** Status as a list, providers and features as lists; a provider opens its sheet (band, key last four, models, used by, this month, deadline, actions), a feature opens its settings sheet; dialogs are bottom sheets; Save changes docks while edits are unsaved.

**Not built as drawn.** Allowing photos to leave the server asked for a confirmation, not a PIN; since 2026-11-14 the save that turns it on asks for the administrator's own PIN (see "First-save drafts and the cloud photo PIN"). A provider's "Test connection" runs a feature test (no provider-only test exists); a provider no feature uses cannot be tested here. The failing card's real-request count covers the last 7 days.

**Verification.** See `docs/qa/recent-changes-review-2026-10-09.md`, "AI configuration page rebuilt (2026-11-15)".

## First-save drafts and the cloud photo PIN (2026-11-14)

Three small decisions the owner left open ("do what's best"). No schema change, no migration.

**New onboarding survey** (`components/v2/admin/onboarding/wizard.tsx`, `lib/onboarding/wizard-draft.ts`). Later saves are as before (Next / Save Draft PATCH). Next or Save Draft on an empty form creates nothing. A failed first save keeps every answer on the page with "Draft not saved yet: <reason>" and Retry, and warns before the tab closes. Every retry sends the same `Idempotency-Key`; `POST /api/admin/onboarding/surveys` keeps it as `adminOverrides.draftCreateKey` and a repeat key from the same person returns the existing draft (200) instead of creating another. Callers without the header (the classic page) behave as before. Checklist Preview and Review say they need the saved draft until it exists. See "No draft for an untouched or offered job" in the shared-draft section. **Cloud photo PIN** (`PUT /api/admin/ai/settings`, `lib/ai/provider/admin.ts`, `components/v2/admin/ai/ai-configuration-workspace.tsx`). Turning "photos may leave the server" ON for any feature needs the administrator's own PIN (their password while they have no PIN), sent as `security` with the routing and verified in the same request by `verifySensitiveAction(…, "ai.cloud_photos")` (new sensitive action and capability `ai.cloud_photos`, tier grant, administrators only: Settings, AI itself stays ADMIN-only, so a grant alone opens nothing). Refused while testing as someone (403), wrong or missing PIN 423 with `needsCredential` and the features; nothing is saved. `saveAiRouting` re-checks under its advisory lock that every feature it turns on was confirmed (else `AiCloudPhotosConfirmationRequired`, 423) and writes `AI_CLOUD_PHOTOS_ALLOWED` beside `AI_SETTINGS_UPDATED`; the PIN check writes `SENSITIVE_ACTION_CONFIRMED`. Turning it off and every other routing change need no PIN. On the page, the switch still asks the ordinary "Allow photos to go to …?" question; Save changes then opens a tier C `EConfirmDialog` ("Let photos leave this server?", naming each feature and provider) only when the save turns the switch on for at least one feature. A refused PIN keeps the dialog with the reason and keeps the draft; a stale save still shows the conflict card.
