Report an item, Edit details, Client price and Link to a job use `EActionDialog`. Every sheet freezes while saving, keeps a failed draft with the server's reason, ignores late answers for another item, and keeps its draft when closed until another item opens.

**Server.** New `GET /api/admin/maintenance` (list, `parseListQuery`, sorts priority/status/title/assigned/visit/cost/reported, unknown filters 400; `lib/maintenance/admin-list.ts`) and `GET /api/admin/maintenance/export` (same filters, CSV, capped at 5000, missing values empty). Both ADMIN/OPS_MANAGER via `requireRole`, mapped to the Maintenance pack by the existing `admin/maintenance` section. `POST /api/maintenance/bulk` now answers per item (`results: [{ id, outcome: done|unchanged|missing, fromStatus }]`, `updated` unchanged) and accepts `{ ids, assign: { workerId } }` (per item done / unchanged / refused with reason). The worker portal notice moved to `lib/maintenance/assign-notice.ts` (behaviour unchanged). `GET /api/admin/maintenance/workers` adds `openItems` and `lastVisitAt` (null when no arrival or clock-in was recorded).

**Not built as drawn.** The Visit sheet has no instructions box (instructions stay in their own card; saving both would be two writes). The Assign sheet has no "Pay, optional" (pay exists only on roster rows once a person is on the item). The phone Filter sheet applies each choice at once (shared `EFilterBar` behaviour) rather than on "Show". The status bar on a phone is chips. No "Mark resolved" photo requirement, instruction photo upload or SMS on assign (open owner questions).

## Simpler confirmations: three tiers, no typed words, PIN or password for sensitive actions (2026-11-14)

Approved board "Confirmations and deletes" (`ConfirmDialogs.dc.html`). Owner: "Redo deleting popups, make them easier with just pin/password for sensitive ones", then "use your defaults and build all designs". No schema change, no migration.

**The three tiers** (shared `EConfirmDialog`, `components/v2/ui/confirm-dialog.tsx`, built on `EActionDialog`; `EConfirmModal` in `estate-kit.tsx` now renders it and keeps its old props):
- **A, ordinary**: one sentence and the confirm button, which has focus (Enter confirms, Escape cancels). `tier="ordinary"`, or `danger={false}` on `EConfirmModal`.
- **B, removes something**: one line saying what is removed and one red button; focus starts on Cancel. Undo (`undoToast`, `components/v2/ui/undo-toast.tsx`, 10 seconds) only where the removal has not left the screen: form builder questions and sections (steps the builder document back only while the removal is still its last change), hiring application sections and quiz questions, QA inspection damage entries and flagged areas, and a plain manual line removed from a DRAFT invoice (added again with the same text, quantity, price and category). Elsewhere the line says "This cannot be undone". `EConfirmModal`'s default.
- **C, sensitive**: one or two plain lines, ONE credential field and the confirm button. `requireSecurity` on `EConfirmModal`, or `tier="sensitive"`. The server verifies the credential with `verifySensitiveAction` in the same request.
- Eyebrow shows the tier letter and its name; the title is a question; the confirm button names the action. Below 640px it is a bottom sheet: Cancel as a text button above a full-width confirm, 44px targets, sticky footer, the credential field scrolled into view when the keyboard opens.
- `confirmPhrase` is accepted and ignored: nobody types DELETE, VOID, REMOVE or DISCARD (it was asked by delete job, delete case, delete client, delete account on the person page and the accounts menu, delete assistant team, delete approval record, reconcile Xero invoice, client remove assistant team, client discard stock count). No route ever checked the word.

**The credential field** (`components/v2/shared/own-pin-fields.tsx`, same exports, so every prompt using `OwnPinFields` / `useOwnPinPrompt` changed with it, including Test as, the page locks, Access save, Agents, job reset, agent requests and clients bulk): always the person actually signed in. States: has a PIN ("Your PIN", number pad, paste, Show, "Forgot it? Change your PIN"); wrong PIN ("That PIN is not right. 3 tries left.", the field cleared, the reason kept); locked ("Locked", "Too many wrong tries. Try again at 14:52." in the organisation timezone, button off); no PIN yet ("Your password", "Set a PIN" link to `/v2/admin/profile#own-pin`); testing as someone else ("Not available", "Stop testing as … to do this."). The tries left, lock and timezone come from `GET /api/me/admin-pin` (now also `attemptsLeft` and `timezone`; while testing its 403 carries `code: "ACTUAL_ACTOR_REQUIRED"`), read again after a failed attempt. A failed save keeps the reason and details and clears the credential.

**Server credential rule** (`lib/security/admin-verification.ts`). Owner default (1), pending owner confirmation: a person with no PIN confirms with their account password alone (before: password plus a new PIN). A password sent with a valid `newPin` still stores it (older prompts). A person WITH a PIN is never accepted with their password (`PIN_REQUIRED`). Lockout unchanged (5 wrong PINs or passwords → 15 minutes, on the row), actual-actor and Test-as refusals unchanged, routes' own rate limits unchanged. Every accepted confirmation writes `SENSITIVE_ACTION_CONFIRMED` (entity `UserSecurityPin`, actual actor) with `{ action, credential: "pin" | "password" | "password_and_new_pin" }`, never the value. `verifySensitiveActionCredential` returns which credential was used; `verifySensitiveAction` still returns `true`. `lib/security/route-verification.ts` (`routeSecurityRefusal`, `securityFromBody`) is the shared route helper: 403 while testing, 423 for a refused credential.

**Reasons** (`lib/confirmations/reasons.ts`, plain module; owner default (5): fixed in the product, not in Settings; picker `components/v2/ui/reason-picker.tsx`). Required as quick picks plus "Other…" with any non-empty text, no minimum length, only for: invoice void and credit-note void (owner default (2), new: `PATCH /api/admin/invoices/[id]` with status VOID requires `voidReason`, written to a new `CLIENT_INVOICE_VOIDED` audit row; the document, its amounts and issued/paid records are unchanged), the reconciled Xero void (10-character minimum removed), laundry run void (3-character minimum removed) and undo void (newly required), changing a decided pay amount and deleting a decided approval record (`POST /api/admin/approvals/history/[id]` now requires `note` for `edit` and `delete`), voiding a damage submission (10-character minimum removed). The two evidence reviews keep a required free-text reason with no minimum: cleaner invoice delivery review and draft evidence review (both routes' 10-character minimum removed; the draft review's browser confirm became a tier A dialog).

**Xero reconcile.** The route still REQUIRES the correction reference (3 to 500 characters), so it stays visible and required in the dialog; only the optional note is under "Add details". The quick pick (plus the note) becomes the stored reason.

**Other defaults applied, pending owner confirmation.** (3) Removing a line from a DRAFT invoice asks for no PIN (tier B, Undo for plain manual lines); `lib/billing/client-invoice-patch.ts` checks DRAFT before the row lock and again under it (approved in between → 409, "no longer a draft"). Lines on invoices past DRAFT still need the PIN. (4) Deleting a cleaner's submitted invoice is tier C: new sensitive action `cleaner_invoices.delete` and capability (Payroll, tier "manage", so who may delete is unchanged) verified by `DELETE /api/admin/cleaner-invoices/[id]` with `{ security }`.

**PIN now verified by the action's own route** (before: only the browser's pre-check against `/api/admin/security/verify`): remove a job extra (`DELETE …/quote-extras`), delete a checklist library module, remove a shopping-run receipt (`PATCH …/shopping-runs/[id]` when the receipt list loses an entry), delete an assistant team and remove an assistant (both `va-teams` routes; the Assistants tab's browser confirm became a tier C dialog), and voiding a damage submission (newly tier C per the board; who may void is unchanged). The classic `/admin/checklists/library` page now collects the credential with the classic confirm dialog (shared field) and sends `{ security }`. Payment gateway delete (`DELETE /api/admin/payment-gateways/[id]`) verifies `{ security }` itself too; the v2 Settings section and the classic gateways page send it.

**AI provider keys.** `POST /api/admin/ai/credentials` confirms with the same credential: `{ provider, apiKey | clear: true, security: { pin } | { password } }`; a top-level `password` from an older screen is read as `security.password` (accepted only while there is no PIN). Refusals answer 423 (403 while testing) with `code` and `needsCredential: true`; the route's 10 per 15 minutes limit and ENCRYPTION_KEY check are unchanged.

**Classic pages and Maintenance (follow-up, same day).** `components/shared/two-step-confirm-dialog.tsx` no longer asks for a typed phrase (`confirmPhrase` / the policy phrase are ignored; no route checks one) and can carry a required quick-pick reason (`reasonChoices`). The classic invoices page voids and deletes through it with the PIN (void with a reason), so those calls are accepted again. Admin Maintenance resolve / dismiss (single and bulk) is a tier A `EConfirmDialog` with the optional note. Not changed: `window.confirm` prompts outside the board's inventory; a classic invoice line removal past DRAFT still sends no PIN and is refused, as before. See the review record for the full inventory.

## Xero connection stays connected (2026-11-15)

**Problem (owner):** "it only connects for 30 mins from xero." Xero access tokens last 30 minutes; a connection stays alive only with the `offline_access` scope, a stored refresh token and a renewal that stores each rotated refresh token (Xero FAQ, developer.xero.com/faq/oauth2, read 2026-11-14: access token 30 minutes, "unused refresh tokens expire after 60 days", replace the refresh token with the one returned; the old one may be retried for a 30-minute grace period).

**Causes found** (proved first by `tests/lib/xero-token-lifecycle.test.ts`, which failed on the old code): (1) connections made before `offline_access` was added (commit 5c6d9c8, 2026-11-11) have an empty refresh token and lapse 30 minutes after connecting, and the status still said "Connected"; (2) no single flight: two calls near expiry (web replicas, the hourly worker, a push that reads the token several times) each exchanged the same refresh token and the last writer won, so the stored rotated token could be the one Xero discards; (3) any refused renewal, including a 503, 429 or network error, was recorded as "sign-in lapsed" and the caller got "No active Xero connection", even with a still-valid access token; (4) a 401 from the API was never renewed and retried; (5) nothing renewed an idle connection, so with nothing to push or check the refresh token would expire after 60 days; (6) tokens were stored in plaintext; the auth URL (with the OAuth state) was logged.

**Token service** (`lib/xero/token-service.ts`; every call in `lib/xero/client.ts` — contact sync, client invoice and credit-note push, cleaner bill push, invoice/credit-note reads, account name — goes through it via one `xeroCall`). Renews when the access token is within 5 minutes of expiry, when Xero answered 401 (`rejectedVersion`: renew unless a newer version exists, then retry the request once with the same Idempotency-Key), or when forced (keep-alive). Single flight across processes: a lease on the `XeroConnection` row taken by compare-and-set on `tokenVersion` (`refreshLockId`/`refreshLockUntil`, 90 s, longer than every attempt); others keep using a still-valid token or wait for the new version. The new access token, refresh token and expiry are written together, encrypted, with `tokenVersion` incremented, conditionally on the version renewed, before the token is returned; a renewal that cannot be stored is never used (Xero's grace period lets the old refresh token be retried). Transient failures (network, timeout, 5xx, 429 with Retry-After up to 20 s) are retried three times with backoff (1 s, 4 s), recorded in `lastRefreshError`, and leave the connection CONNECTED; terminal ones set `status = NEEDS_RECONNECT` with `statusReasonCode` (`REFRESH_REJECTED` for invalid_grant, `APP_CREDENTIALS_REJECTED` for invalid_client/unauthorized_client, `NO_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `TENANT_REMOVED`) and `statusReason`, keep the row and its tokens for audit, and stop renewing until a reconnect. A 403, or a 401 after renewal, checks `GET /connections`; the organisation missing → `TENANT_REMOVED`. Missing Client ID/Secret, a missing `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (checked before calling Xero, so a rotated token can never be lost) or an unreadable stored token are configuration failures and change no status.

**Encryption.** Tokens were plaintext; they are now stored with the existing `encryptSecret` (`enc:v1`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`). Existing rows are read as plaintext (`decryptSecret` passes them through) and become encrypted on their next renewal or reconnect. Connect refuses with a clear reason when `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is absent. No token or OAuth state is logged; reasons are one line with bearer tokens and long opaque strings redacted.

**Connect, disconnect.** The callback stores the granted scopes (token response `scope`), status CONNECTED, `connectedAt`, increments `tokenVersion` (an in-flight renewal of the old sign-in cannot overwrite it) and deactivates any other active connection, so one is used. Disconnect revokes the decrypted refresh token with the app's credentials (Basic) and deactivates the row.

**Keep-alive.** Worker job `xero-token-keepalive`, daily 03:47 Australia/Sydney (`SNEEK_DISABLED_JOBS`/`SNEEK_ENABLED_JOBS` apply): forced renewal through the token service (records `lastRefreshedAt`), organisation check (`lastTenantCheckAt`), and a retry of a reconnect notice that could not be queued. A NEEDS_RECONNECT connection is not sent to Xero.

**Status** (`lib/xero/connection-status.ts`, `GET /api/xero/status` adds the organisation timezone). States: connected; attention (the last renewal failed, retried automatically — never shown as plainly connected; the Finance header shows "Xero status unknown"); reconnect-once (no refresh token: "Reconnect Xero once to keep it connected" — an existing connection made without `offline_access` cannot be upgraded silently); needs-reconnect (with the reason). Settings › Xero (`components/v2/admin/settings/xero-connection-card.tsx`) shows the organisation, connected since, last refreshed, next refresh (the access token's renewal point, or the next Xero call after it), the keep-alive schedule, the 60-day "must renew by" date, the last attempt, and Reconnect (primary when reconnecting is required) and Disconnect; times in the organisation timezone; a failed status read says so instead of "Not connected".

**Notice.** `xero.reconnect_needed` (catalog Money; wording `XERO_RECONNECT_WORDING`, editable): INBOX only through the intent pipeline to active administrators, scope STAFF_MEMBER per person, severity ACTION, opens Settings › Xero. Once per outage: only the process whose compare-and-set moves CONNECTED → NEEDS_RECONNECT claims `reconnectNoticeAt` and sends; event id `xero-reconnect:{connection}:{needsReconnectAt}`; a failed queue releases the claim for the keep-alive to retry. Queued is not delivered.

**Not changed.** What is pushed to Xero, any money arithmetic, issued/paid records. Pushes that failed because the sign-in had lapsed stay retryable through the existing paths with the same idempotency key (client invoices: FAILED reservation → Retry Xero; cleaner bills: XERO_EXPORTING → push again); nothing is re-sent automatically.

**Schema.** Migration `20261115050000_xero_token_lifecycle` adds `tokenVersion`, `status`, `statusReasonCode`, `statusReason`, `needsReconnectAt`, `reconnectNoticeAt`, `connectedAt` (backfilled from `createdAt`), `lastRefreshedAt` (from `lastSyncAt`, which only a renewal wrote), `lastRefreshAttemptAt`, `lastRefreshError`, `lastTenantCheckAt`, `refreshLockId`, `refreshLockUntil`; an active row with no refresh token and an expired access token becomes NEEDS_RECONNECT / NO_REFRESH_TOKEN (its notice is sent by the first keep-alive). `lastSyncAt` is still written on renewal for older readers.

**After deploy (owner).** Make sure `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set on the web and worker containers. Reconnect Xero once in Settings › Xero (a connection made before `offline_access` has no refresh token). In the Xero developer portal the app must be a Web app (auth code flow, not a Custom Connection) whose redirect URI is exactly `{site}/api/xero/callback`; no scope setting is needed there (scopes are requested at connect). Then retry any failed pushes from the invoice lists.

**Not verified.** Nothing ran against real Xero (no credentials in this environment); the exact error bodies Xero returns for a revoked token, a removed organisation (assumed 403 → connection list check) and rate-limited renewals are from the documentation and OAuth standards, not observed. The settings card was checked in jsdom component tests only, not in a browser.

## Sending safeguards and the repeated-email audit (2026-11-15)

Owner report: "some cleaners are getting constant emails". No production logs were available; the causes below come from a code audit of every worker job, sweep and send path. Since 2026-11-10 (`scripts/embedded-worker.cjs`) every deployment runs the worker, so sweeps that had not run since 4 October all started at once. Migration `20261115060000_sending_safeguards` (additive).

**Causes found and fixed, most likely first (each has a regression test that fails on the previous code):**
1. **QA auto-score re-scored failed jobs every hour** (`lib/qa/auto-score.ts`, worker `qa-auto-score`, hourly, on by default). A failed automatic score sends the job back to QA_REVIEW, which the sweep scores again (only a real "QA" inspection excluded a job). Every hour it filed another AUTO review and sent every cleaner on the job the "QA needs attention" inbox notice, push, **email and SMS**, until someone inspected the job, for up to 200 jobs per run. Now each submission is auto-scored once: the sweep skips jobs with an AUTO/ADMIN review newer than the latest submission, re-checked under the per-job lock (`ALREADY_SCORED`). A rework resubmission is scored again; an administrator's quick score is never blocked. Test: `tests/lib/qa-auto-score-once.test.ts`.
2. **Tomorrow's-jobs summary could repeat to every cleaner** (`lib/ops/tomorrow-prep.ts`, every 2 h after the configured time). It emails and texts every active cleaner and laundry user, and recorded the day as done only after the last one. A run that failed part-way left the day unrecorded and the next tick sent to everyone again. Each person is now claimed once per part and day (`dispatchNotificationOnce`) before sending. A manual "send now" is unchanged. **Behaviour change, pending owner confirmation:** a cleaner or driver with nothing tomorrow now gets the inbox notice only, with no email or SMS (previously a daily "no jobs tomorrow" email and SMS to every cleaner). Test: `tests/lib/tomorrow-prep-once.test.ts`.
3. **24-hour and 2-hour job reminders recorded "sent" after sending** (`lib/ops/reminders.ts`, every 30 min). The flag was set only after a clear provider yes. An uncertain answer or a failed flag update meant another email or SMS every 30 minutes for the whole window. The job is now claimed first (conditional update). The claim is released only when nothing reached a provider (switched off, no key, refused before sending). Test: `tests/lib/job-reminders-claim.test.ts`.
4. **Client follow-ups queued twice sent twice** (`lib/ops/follow-up-sequences.ts`, `lib/notifications/client-automation.ts`): pg-boss `singletonKey`, plus a send-once receipt per job and step or rule. Test: `tests/lib/follow-up-once.test.ts`.
5. **Daily unfinished-job push never stopped** for a job left PAUSED (`lib/ops/unfinished-reminders.ts`). It now stops after 3 nights per job; the office still sees the job.
6. **Direct Twilio call** in the finance template engine (`lib/notifications/engine.ts`) bypassed every SMS gate. It now goes through `sendSmsDetailed`.
Checked and not repeating: cleaner day reminder (receipt), missed clock-in (one per job), auto clock-out / auto-pause (claimed state change), case follow-up (48 h stale window), iCal booking-moved and removed notices (assignment removed), location notices (inbox only, event ids), workforce posts (marked), job-task auto-approve (state change first), document expiry (weekly), the intent pipeline (one intent per transport and person; UNCERTAIN never retried; MAX attempts), mobile outbox (claimed). The worker's handler wrapper never lets pg-boss retry a job.

**The gate (one place every outbound message passes).** `lib/notifications/safeguards/gate.ts` `guardOutbound`, called immediately before the provider call in the only four modules allowed to reach a provider: `email.ts` (per address), `sms.ts`, `web-push.ts` (one decision per person, per device for pipeline intents), `mobile-push.ts`. The inbox is never capped. `tests/lib/outbound-provider-imports.test.ts` fails if any other file imports Resend, Twilio, web-push or nodemailer, or calls their APIs. Decisions are taken in a transaction under an advisory lock per (transport group, person) and written as `OutboundMessageEvent` rows. Caps, duplicates and the breaker count these rows, so they are correct across web replicas and the worker (tested with real concurrency). Producers may pass `safeguard: { typeKey, entityKey, recipientUserId }` (delivery.ts `typeKey`, office sends and pipeline intents do this automatically). Otherwise the type comes from the event key, subject, email kind or category, and the catch-all is `unclassified:<transport>`.

Order of rules (`decide.ts`): disabled account, emergency stop, pause (type / person / subject), identical duplicate, same type and subject, alert limit, hourly ceiling, daily ceiling, quiet hours. Classes (`classify.ts`):
- SECURITY: `account.security`, `account.invitations`, any `critical` email. Exempt from everything but the duplicate check.
- ALERT: the safeguards' own notice. Exempt from pauses and ceilings; at most N emails per hour.
- URGENT: cancellations, job changes, offers, day/2-hour reminders, clock changes, field and iCal alerts, client job updates. No quiet hours and no same-subject window.
- BULK: marketing campaigns. Never pause a type.
- NORMAL: everything else.

A suppressed message is **never delivered**. Callers get `ok: false, skipped: true, suppressed: { reason, held }` (SMS `status: "suppressed"`) and record "Not sent (sending safeguard): <reason>" with `deliveryStatus` SUPPRESSED or HELD. The event row has no outcome. When the gate itself cannot run, NORMAL and BULK messages are not sent (`SAFEGUARD_UNAVAILABLE`); security, urgent and alert messages go. **Deploy the migration before the code.**

**Defaults (all pending owner confirmation; editable by ADMIN with PIN inside the bounds shown on the screen):**

| | Email | SMS | Push (browser + phone) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Per person per hour | 15 | 6 | 30 |
| Per person per day | 50 | 15 | 120 |
| Same type and subject once per | 30 min | 60 min | 5 min |
| Breaker: attempts to one person in 15 min | 12 | 6 | 30 |

Other limits:
- Identical message dropped within 12 h.
- Breaker window 15 min. Breaker per type: 200 attempts on one transport in the window. Breaker per job or subject: 40.
- Most recipients in one send: 25 (the whole send is refused).
- Safeguard alert emails: 6 per hour in total.
- Quiet hours for staff: 21:00 to 07:00 in the organisation timezone (clients and the public are never held).

Sanity check: a cleaner on six jobs gets about 25 to 30 automatic emails a day across offers, reminders, QA and changes.

**Breaker and alert.** Attempts in the window, sent or not, are counted for the person, the subject and the type (catch-all types are never paused as a type). Crossing a threshold opens one `OutboundSafeguardIncident` (advisory lock per scope). It pauses email, SMS and push for that scope; the inbox continues. Its creator alone tells every active administrator through `sendOfficeNotification`: one inbox notice and one email (event `safeguard:<incident>`). The notice says what tripped, how many, to whom (masked) and links to the screen. **A pause never resumes on its own:** only an administrator's Resume ends it (no silent cool-down). A worker job failing 3 times in a row opens a non-pausing incident and one alert; it closes when the job succeeds (`lib/ops/worker-guard.ts`). The guard also skips a tick while the previous run of the same job is still going after its timeout.

**Emergency stop.** One switch (AppSetting `notificationSafeguards`): ADMIN, own PIN (`routeSecurityRefusal` / `verifySensitiveAction`), refused while impersonating, audited `NOTIFICATION_EMERGENCY_STOP_ON` / `_OFF`. While on, only security messages leave; the inbox works. Per-type pause and resume: ADMIN, not impersonating, audited `NOTIFICATION_TYPE_PAUSED` / `NOTIFICATION_SAFEGUARD_RESUMED`; no PIN (pausing only makes things safer). Limits: ADMIN with PIN, stale-write 409, out-of-bounds 400, audited `NOTIFICATION_SAFEGUARDS_UPDATED`.

**Quiet hours.** Non-urgent email and SMS to staff is HELD: the payload is kept on the event row, released once after quiet hours by the worker, re-checked by the gate (duplicates, pauses and preferences still apply), and dropped as `HELD_EXPIRED` after 12 h. Push at night and these types are DROPPED (inbox kept): `job.reminder.unfinished_daily`, `job.reminder.manual`, `laundry.cleaner_nudge`, `office.sla_and_summaries`, `stock.alerts`, location notices. Emails with attachments are never held.

**Also.**
- Disabled accounts are refused (except security).
- The send-size cap applies.
- `SNEEK_OUTBOUND_SANDBOX_EMAIL` (non-production) sends every email to one inbox marked with the real recipients; `SNEEK_OUTBOUND_SANDBOX_SMS=off` sends no SMS.
- Existing person preferences, `allEmailOff`, kind switches and the Resend bounce/complaint suppression list still run first.

**Worker job** `notification-safeguards`, every 10 min: expire and release held messages, keep events for 35 days, and once a day after 08:00 an inbox-only line to administrators when something was not sent or tripped the day before (claimed per day).

**Screen.** `/v2/admin/notifications/safeguards` ("Sending safeguards", settings catalog › Notifications; one h1; Estate primitives; stacked rows below 640px). It shows the emergency stop, what is paused (with Resume) and pausing a type, today's sent / not sent / held by type and transport, most-messaged people, reasons, recent "not sent" (masked addresses, organisation timezone), limits and recent incidents. Reads: ADMIN, and OPS_MANAGER with the notifications pack (middleware; the routes re-check the role). Changes: ADMIN only. Routes: `GET|PATCH /api/admin/notifications/safeguards`, `POST …/emergency-stop`, `POST …/pauses`. Command's work queue shows a "sending-paused" card (urgency now, needs the communications pack) while the emergency stop is on or anything is paused. New catalog type `system.sending_safeguard` (`catalog-safeguards.ts`, wording `definitions/safeguards.ts`).

**What the owner should do in production now.**
- Before deploy: set `SNEEK_DISABLED_JOBS=qa-auto-score,tomorrow-prep-dispatch` on the worker or web container (whichever runs the worker) and restart. Optionally also set `reminder-dispatch` there. Or turn off QA automation's auto-score in Settings.
- After deploy: run `npx prisma migrate deploy` first. Remove those entries from `SNEEK_DISABLED_JOBS`. Watch the Sending safeguards screen. Use the emergency stop if anything still loops.

**Not built.**
- Per-person unsubscribe link in operational emails (the footer links to Email preferences instead). Campaign emails have a signed one-click unsubscribe since 2026-11-16 (see "Email design system").
- Bounce/complaint auto-pause beyond the existing suppression list.
- Holding push at night (dropped instead).
- Moving the remaining direct producers onto the intent pipeline (the gate covers them).
- A per-type editable quiet-hours policy (it is in code, documented above).
- Admin alerts by SMS.

## Damage report record page and New invoice panel (2026-11-15, boards "Damage report" and "New invoice")

Owner: "build designs with my defaults". No schema change, no migration.

**Damage report record page** (`/v2/admin/damage/[reportId]`, `components/v2/admin/damage/*`; ADMIN and OPS_MANAGER as before, the Cases pack through middleware and the live role guard on every call). Built like the Maintenance item page: back link to the job, one h1 "Damage at <property>" with the status and highest severity, Download PDF, the one primary decision and More ▾ (Preview as the client, Close without releasing…, Download PDF, Copy link, then Send back to the cleaner…; footnote "No delete"). A progress strip from stored state only (`damageRecordStages`, `lib/damage/record-model.ts`): submitted, sent back, office review, released, acknowledged, closed. Six fact tiles; "Our repair estimate" is the sum of the items that have an estimate (whole cents, `summariseEstimates`) and always says how many items it covers ("2 of 3 items · 1 not estimated"); with none it reads "Not estimated", never $0. Item cards: tone band for major/severe (problem) or an unestimated item (attention); the cleaner's words; photos in section order labelled (Overview, Close-up · marked up, …); Preview shows the untouched original (`DamageItemPhoto.s3Key`, ADMIN view model `originalUrl`) beside the flattened marked-up copy (`flatKey`, `markedUpUrl`); the client view model carries neither field. Case and repair read live; "Earlier reports here" when no repair is linked. The estimate saves when the field is left (existing SET_COST, now scoped to the report's own items and logged `DAMAGE_ITEM_ESTIMATE_SET`); frozen while saving, a refusal keeps the typed value with Retry. The item's own case history sits under it. History card (organisation timezone): submissions (`DAMAGE_REPORT_SUBMITTED`, written after each submit from now on; older reports fall back to the stored submission time and the time their cases were opened), send-backs, decisions (`DAMAGE_REPORT_RELEASED`, `_TAKEN_BACK`, `_CLOSED`, `_CLOSED_RELEASED`, `_REOPENED`, written in the review transaction), estimate changes, the release message and the client's sign-off. Loading shows the page outline; a report that cannot be opened says "This damage report is not available to you" and links back to the job.

Decision rail: three plain choices while under review (release; close without releasing = the existing REVIEW `{ release: false, close: true }`; send back). Released: take back, close, send back. Closed: reopen (REVIEW keeping visibility), take back when visible. Sent back (DRAFT): no decision until resubmitted. Send back is tier C on the shared `EConfirmDialog` (new optional `lead` slot draws the two modes before the reason): mode, quick-pick reason (`REASON_CHOICES.damageVoid`), the person's own PIN verified by the damage route with `verifySensitiveAction` in the same request (unchanged server rule); a refusal keeps mode and reason and clears the PIN. Release, take back, close and reopen are tier A. "What the client will see" → Preview renders `GET …?view=client` (`getDamageClientPreview`, the CLIENT view model: no estimates, internal transition notes, reviewer or send-back history) in the client page's own component, read only (no acknowledge). Linked records: clean, property, client, each item's case, each repair. Phones: stage strip swipes, figures fold, History / What the client will see / Linked records fold, More is a sheet, the primary decision docks.

**Release message** (new catalog type `client.damage_released`, `lib/damage/release-notice.ts`, wording editable in Notifications). Owner default, pending confirmation: inbox and email ticked, SMS off; the office chooses transports on each release ("Tell the client" card with the exact wording from `?view=release-notice`). Inbox = the client's inbox row only (office pipeline `INBOX`, never a push); email through the office pipeline (queued, or the direct send while the email outbox transport is off); SMS through the SMS chokepoint once per request key, re-checking scope just before the provider. Recipients: active CLIENT logins of the job's client (scope `JOB_CLIENT_CONTACT`). Refused before anything is released when the client switched notifications off or has no login, and while testing as someone else; unavailable transports are unticked and disabled with the reason. The message is sent after the release commits; a failed message never undoes the release and says nothing was sent. Outcomes are the transports' own states (queued, in the inbox, accepted by the provider), audited `DAMAGE_RELEASE_NOTICE_SENT` once per key; never "read". Who may release is unchanged (owner default: anyone with Cases access). Airbnb Resolution Centre claims were not built (owner default: keep them in case notes).

**New invoice panel** (`/v2/admin/finance/invoices/new`, `components/v2/admin/finance/invoices/new-invoice/*`; ADMIN, and OPS_MANAGER with finance to open and finance manage to create, `newInvoiceAccess`). One page for From finished jobs, Blank invoice and Credit note (needs the void and credit notes right, says so otherwise). "New invoice ▾", the phone chooser and old `?new=jobs|blank|credit` links open it (`?kind=`). Choices keep their fields while another is shown.

From finished jobs: client, property, period, bill jobs by, GST (the old generator dialog's options). Period default (owner default, pending confirmation; `lib/billing/invoice-period-default.ts`): the day after the client's last live invoice's period end to today, else the 1st of the month; organisation calendar days. "What the draft will hold" (`GET /api/admin/invoices/generate?view=preview`, `lib/billing/client-invoice-generate-preview.ts`) runs the generator's own selection and line builders, now exported from `client-invoices.ts` (`loadGeneratorJobs`, `buildGeneratorJobLines`, `loadGeneratorExtraLines`, `combineGeneratorLines`; `generateClientInvoice` uses the same functions, behaviour unchanged), without writing. Jobs grouped by property with the charge source (property rate; fixed price with its invoice note and a public holiday rate snapshot when applied; price book), the amount ex GST, the generator's other lines (shopping, client-paid repairs), totals from `calculateShoppingAwareInvoiceTotals`, and what was left out (already on a live invoice with its number, cancelled, skipped). A job with no rate shows "No charge" (never $0) with two fixes in place: Set a rate (`PUT /api/admin/property-client-rates`) and Give the job a fixed price (`PATCH /api/admin/jobs/[id]` with `expectedUpdatedAt`); the preview reloads. The draft stays blocked, as the generator does, unless the office ticks "Create without J-…" (owner default, pending confirmation): `generateClientInvoice({ leaveOutUnratedJobIds })` leaves exactly those jobs off and records them in `metadata.notBilled`; any other unrated job still refuses. The editor shows them as "Not billed: no rate". Create draft: `POST /api/admin/invoices/generate` with a request key (`lib/billing/client-invoice-generate-request.ts`): RUNNING/FINISHED/FAILED rows in AuditLog under an advisory lock, a repeat key returns the same draft, a key reused with another selection is refused, a refused generation may retry with the same key; the browser guards a double click and keeps the key and selection after a failure. Without a key the route behaves as before. The draft is the existing generator's (parity test). "Ready to bill, all clients" with the existing batch "Create N drafts" sits beside it (N = clients that can be billed). Phones: one card per job, Create draft docked.

Not built as drawn: the board's single period control is two date fields with a formatted line beneath; the Ready to bill card has no date range (its figure is all finished unbilled work, not period bound); no case numbers exist, so cases are linked as "Case for item N"; item titles are area and category (there is no separate short title).

## Property onboarding workspace and client link (2026-11-16, boards "Property onboarding", "Property onboarding steps", "M-PropertyOnboarding")

Owner: "property onboarding steps more easier and advanced way"; build the approved designs with the owner's defaults. Migration `20261116050000_onboarding_workspace` (additive).

**Owner defaults applied, pending owner confirmation.** (1) Access is required before activation. (2) Clients may type access codes through their link; codes are encrypted at once and must be reviewed by the office ("Mark code reviewed") before activation. (3) A client rate (above zero) for the main job type (the first ticked) is required before activation. (4) Laundry partners: left as today. The existing access model has an audience per access-guide entry but no time window for laundry, so "lockbox only on run days" cannot be expressed safely; laundry still reads guide entries (never the stored lockbox, door or alarm code columns) and the workspace says so. (5) Standard stock lists for 1, 2 and 3+ bedrooms (`lib/onboarding/workspace/stock-lists.ts`, default catalog SKUs; fixed in code, not edited in Stock). (6) "Also create first draft jobs" defaults off when a calendar link is saved, on without one. (7) Client link: no login, 7 days by default (1–30), revocable. (8) The office is told the client finished by inbox only. (9) Empty drafts from the old open-to-create page: an ADMIN-only "Review empty drafts" on the list; nothing is deleted automatically.

**Data.** `PropertyOnboardingSurvey` gains `revision` (bumped by every saved change; the stale-save check), `workspace` JSON (rooms list and note, access entries with encrypted codes, stock list, reference photos, rates, hazards and building rules, laundry bag, clock-in radius, job-time source, skipped steps; shape and reader in `lib/onboarding/workspace/types.ts`, missing numbers stay null), `lastSavedAt/ById/Source`. New `OnboardingAnswerRevision` (who changed which fields, `source` ADMIN_CREATED = office or CLIENT_SUBMITTED = the client's link, the existing unused enum value; codes recorded only as "[encrypted]") and `OnboardingClientLink` (HMAC-SHA256 of the token keyed with `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, sections, transport, masked recipient, expiry, revoke, opened/finished times, provider state). Every existing field keeps its storage (`lib/onboarding/workspace/values.ts`): the room note IS `scenarios.bedConfig` (the migration also copies existing text into the room list's note; nothing is discarded); pets, bins and parking stay in `scenarios`.

**Screens.** `/v2/admin/onboarding`: tabs All open / In progress / Waiting on client (open, unfinished client link) / Ready to activate / Activated, 30 days / Rejected with server counts (`GET /api/admin/onboarding/board`), search, Source and Started by filters, readiness bar and percentage, the next missing item, last saved (organisation timezone), row tint (honey waiting, sage ready), checklist preview of the selected row from 1280 px, phone cards with the title band and the docked "+ Start". `/v2/admin/onboarding/new`: nothing is created on opening; the first autosave after a name or address creates the draft with the existing Idempotency-Key route, then the URL becomes `/v2/admin/onboarding/<OB number>#basics`. Old `/new?edit=<id>` links redirect to the workspace; `[id]` accepts the id or the OB number. `/v2/admin/onboarding/<OB>`: checklist (done / required / recommended / C client asked), one step in the middle, "This step sets up" on the right, answer history; 11 steps in any order with per-field autosave (on leaving a field; `PATCH …/workspace` with the revision seen), a save chip (Saving…, Saved hh:mm, Not saved + Retry; the failed change stays queued and leaving warns), and "X changed <step> at hh:mm. Your edit is kept. Compare" when someone else saved the same step since. Fields are not frozen while saving (board: "Fields never freeze except during Activate"). Step 12 Readiness lists exactly what is missing, what activation creates, Activate (tier A) and Reject (tier A with reason picks `onboardingReject`), then the activated result (warnings, Open property, Create first job). Phone: the checklist is the menu; a step opens full screen with Previous / Next docked above the tab bar.

**Activation** (`POST …/activate`, `lib/onboarding/workspace/activate.ts`, ADMIN and OPS_MANAGER as the approve route): readiness is checked on the server; a newer revision than the one on screen is refused (409); a draft is submitted and then the EXISTING `approveSurvey` runs (client, property, geocode, encrypted codes, access guide, calendar link saved switched off, laundry run, checklist profile and forms, default stock, first jobs). Two optional inputs were added to `approveSurvey`, absent for every older caller: `afterPropertyCreated` (runs in the approval transaction before APPROVED is stamped: workspace access entries into the guide without codes and codes into the encrypted columns only where empty, hazards and building rules into the guide and notes, room list into notes, reference photos into the setup guide, clock-in radius, sofa beds, bag, job-time source, per-clean cleaner pay of the main type, client rates) and `stockList` (rows with the office's par and reorder levels instead of the whole default set; a row with no par level is not created and is reported; a missing reorder level uses the catalog's level and is reported). On hand cannot be empty in `PropertyStock`, so it starts at the par level as the existing seeding does. Safe to press twice.

**Client link** (`lib/onboarding/workspace/client-link.ts`). The office ticks parts (Access, Photos per room, House rules and hazards, Linen counts, Calendar link; never pricing, rates, laundry partner or the form), recipient, days and Email or SMS explicitly; sent through the shared external-recipient path (new kind `onboarding.client_link`, catalog type, rate limits, masked audit, provider accepted is not delivered); refused while testing as someone else or when the provider is not configured. Public page `/onboarding-link/<token>` (middleware allows the prefix; APIs under `/api/public/onboarding-link/<token>`): the survey comes from the token alone; 60 requests a minute per link and address, 600 an hour per link; refused links say one sentence; the page holds only the ticked parts, only the client's own access entries (office entries as a count, no existing code ever), office photos as "already has a photo". Client saves go through the same section service as `CLIENT_SUBMITTED`, cannot touch office entries (403) or unticked parts (403); photos are images under the link's own key prefix. "I'm finished" records once and queues `onboarding.client_finished`, an INBOX-only pipeline notice to active administrators and operations managers (STAFF_MEMBER scope, editable wording); it activates nothing.

**Not built as drawn.** Calendar is saved switched off on activation, as today (the board says "on, first sync within the hour"); the office turns it on from the property. Laundry run-day lockbox access (see default 4). "Edited in Stock" for standard lists. On hand "Not counted yet" after activation. Listing-URL import (future idea, not built). The 13-step wizard (`components/v2/admin/onboarding/wizard.tsx`, `survey-detail.tsx`) is no longer routed in v2 but kept; the classic `/admin/onboarding` pages are unchanged.

**Verification.** See `docs/qa/recent-changes-review-2026-10-09.md`, "Property onboarding workspace and client link (2026-11-16)".


## Email design system: one layout, blocks, Email look, editor (2026-11-16)

Owner request: "generate designs for email templates as well, more modern and simple standard designs for everything and no more hard coded designs, all editable", built with the owner's defaults. Approved boards "Email design system", "Email catalogue", "Email editor", "Email editor, phone". **No schema change** (designs and the look are AppSetting rows, the reset link reuses `VerificationToken`, the opt-out reuses `EmailSuppression`).

**One renderer** (`lib/email-design/`, plain modules unless noted). An email is a document (`types.ts`): subject, preheader, an optional header reference value and typed blocks: heading, paragraph, details, line items, button, callout (note / action needed / problem / done, word always shown), photo strip, code, signature, divider, secondary note; header and footer are the fixed layout. Inline text is segments (text, bold, value chips); text an editor types is never parsed, so "{{" or "<" stays text; there is no HTML mode. `render.ts` outputs Outlook-safe table HTML (600 attribute, fluid to 320, inline styles, VML button, no flex/grid/CSS variables, en-AU), a dark stylesheet (`prefers-color-scheme` and Outlook.com `data-ogsc`) from the derived palette (`scheme: "dark"` inlines it for previews) and the plain-text part. Every value is escaped; links only http(s)/mailto/tel; "built" values are fragments code built and escaped (tomorrow's lists, QA issues, bulk offer list). Values are a typed allowlist per email (`catalog/*.ts`); an empty optional value hides its details row or uses its fallback ("Not known" by default); an empty **required** value shows "[Label missing]" in preview and makes the send refuse (`missing`). Footer: company name, ABN, address and phone from Company details, the optional extra line, the why-line and "Email preferences" (security emails: "Security emails can't be turned off.", no preferences link; campaigns: "Unsubscribe").

**Send path.** Code builds an email as before (`renderEmailTemplate`, `buildDesignedEmail`, `wrapEmailHtml`, wording-layer fragments) and calls `sendEmailDetailed`; a rendered design carries a spec comment (`spec.ts`). `send-render.ts` (server-only), called by `lib/notifications/email.ts` after the existing preference/audience/suppression gates and **before** the sending safeguards, renders every email again: published version (or the standard), published Email look, current Company details; a raw-HTML template an admin edited keeps its body on the new layout until a block version is published; any other HTML body goes on the layout; a full document with no spec is sent as is. It adds `text` and, for campaigns, `List-Unsubscribe` headers; it strips the spec. Missing required values: `{ ok: false, error: "Not sent: required values are missing (…)", acceptance: NOT_ACCEPTED }`, no gate event, no provider call, logged. From: Email look sender name + the EMAIL_FROM address. Reply-to (owner default): the Email look reply-to, else Company details accounts email (the office inbox); security emails never set one; a caller's explicit reply-to wins. When and to whom nothing changed. The provider-import scan still passes (no provider import outside the four sender modules).

**Email look** (`theme.ts`, page `/v2/admin/notifications/email-look`, settings catalog "Email look" in Company & brand). Logo and dark logo (links; empty = Company & brand logos), brand colour from five checked presets (Forest #1E4A38 default, Harbour, Eucalypt, Ink, Shiraz) or a custom colour that must give button text 4.5:1 (refused otherwise, nearest passing shade suggested), button shape, serif/sans headings, sender name, reply-to, one extra footer line (140). Text, callout and dark colours are fixed and checked (`themeContrastReport`). Reads ADMIN and OPS_MANAGER (communications pack); draft, publish and test ADMIN only; publish with own PIN.

**Store** (`store.ts`, server-only): the wording store's pattern, own rows: `emailDesign:<key>` and `emailLook` with revision, draft, published version and the last 60 versions; advisory lock, revision guard (409), idempotency keys on draft saves and publishes. Version 1 is the standard (code). Restore and Reset make drafts only. Audits: `EMAIL_DESIGN_PUBLISHED` (document, change, actor role), `EMAIL_DESIGN_RESTORED_AS_DRAFT`, `EMAIL_DESIGN_RESET_TO_STANDARD_DRAFT`, `EMAIL_DESIGN_DRAFT_DISCARDED`, `EMAIL_DESIGN_TEST_SENT`, `EMAIL_LOOK_PUBLISHED`. A published version that no longer passes its checks is ignored at send (standard used, logged).

**Editor** (Notifications › Types and wording: the type's details show "Email design" with its emails; `?type=…&email=<key>` opens `components/v2/admin/notifications/email/email-design-editor.tsx` in the same tab, one h1 on the page). Email picker grouped, subject/preheader and block fields with value chips, only the blocks the type allows (with reasons), Alt+↑/↓ and arrow buttons, checks list (errors block publishing: unknown value, required value removed, second button, locked block removed or changed, title not first, empty block, contrast; notes: subject over 50, preheader over 90, long label), preview Desktop/Phone (frame scaled to fit)/Dark/Plain text with sample picker and missing-values switch (the real renderer in a sandboxed frame), "Send test to me", versions with Restore as draft, Reset to standard (tier B), Discard (tier B), Publish (tier C, shared `EConfirmDialog`, change summary). Draft autosaves (1.2 s, one request at a time, retry keeps its key, 409 stops autosave and asks). Phone below 640px: one column, block fields in a bottom sheet, Preview/Publish bar. Security emails show their blocks locked with the reason.

**Who** (`permission.ts`, owner default): drafts, restore/reset into a draft and tests: ADMIN, or OPS_MANAGER with communications at Manage (the wording rule); publishing ADMIN only, own PIN in the same request (`routeSecurityRefusal` → `verifySensitiveAction`), never while impersonating. Test: only to the signed-in person's own account address (looked up by id), "[Test]", invented samples, through `sendEmailDetailed` with safeguard meta (type, `email-design-test:<key>`, own id). Routes: `GET /api/admin/notifications/email-designs`, `GET|PUT …/email-designs/[key]`, `POST …/[key]/publish`, `POST …/[key]/test`, `GET|PUT /api/admin/notifications/email-look`, `POST …/email-look/publish`, `POST …/email-look/test` (communications pack by prefix).

**What moved (version 1 = current words).** Blocks: the 30 shared templates (all callers of `renderEmailTemplate`), the two-step sign-in code, confirm code, recovery link, administrator 2FA reset notice, the invitation link (`lib/auth/invitations.ts`), the password reset (self, office and administrator), the bulk job-offer digest (sentences still from wording `job.offer`), the QA result (`qa-result-email.ts`, same facts, subject and text), and the new Xero reconnect email. The wording editor no longer saves raw HTML for a shared template that has a design (`WordingMovedToDesignError`, 409; Reset still allowed). Intentional wording changes: the sign-up code is no longer in the subject; the sign-in subject reads "Your sNeek Property Services sign-in code". **On the new layout, body still HTML (old path, still editable where it was):** wording-layer email parts (client job updates, job changed/cancelled, cleaner day reminder, office alerts, safeguard alerts, workforce, stock and shopping, laundry team requests, VA and QA invites…), route/library bodies via `wrapEmailHtml` (maintenance assignment, quote extras) or bare fragments (case, shopping, PO, supplier, laundry report routes), lifecycle emails (Forms) and finance-editor emails (`engine.ts`, not sent today), campaigns (designer blocks converted to blocks at send; raw HTML campaigns as a body). **Unchanged:** full HTML documents sent with no spec (e.g. the Monthly Insights report) and the classic settings editor's raw template editor (an edit there puts that email back on its HTML body).

**Owner defaults (pending owner confirmation).** Estate deep green; presets plus a contrast-checked custom colour; client and staff replies to the office inbox (reply-to), no reply-to on security emails; sign-in code not in the subject; invoice PDF still attached; operations managers draft and test only; publishing allowed from a phone with the same PIN; the Xero reconnect alert also emailed to administrators once per outage (`lib/xero/reconnect-notice.ts`: transports `INBOX` and `EMAIL` explicit, catalog `PIPELINE_WITH_FALLBACK`); campaign one-click unsubscribe.

**Campaign unsubscribe** (`unsubscribe.ts`, `app/api/public/unsubscribe`). Campaign sends pass `marketing: true` (`campaign-sender.ts`, `email-campaigns.ts`, the campaign test send). The footer link and `List-Unsubscribe` (+ `List-Unsubscribe-Post: One-Click`) carry an HMAC token (EMAIL_UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET or NEXTAUTH_SECRET) naming the address and purpose "marketing"; no secret or no absolute app URL: mailto only. GET shows a confirm page (scanners do not unsubscribe); POST records `EmailSuppression` reason `MARKETING_OPT_OUT` (never weakening a bounce or complaint, never touching `User.emailStatus`). `isSuppressed` ignores that reason, so job, invoice, account and security email continue; `isMarketingSuppressed` (campaign senders and `sendEmailDetailed` with `marketing`) honours it.

**Administrator password reset** (`app/api/admin/users/[id]/reset-password`). Now emails a single-use, 30-minute link (hashed token, `issueRecoveryToken("pwreset")`, the same link as Forgot password) instead of a temporary password. The account is secured as before (old password replaced by an unusable hash, sessions and remembered devices removed, `requiresPasswordReset`). At most 3 per person per 15 minutes (counted from the audit log), PIN-confirmed, audited `RESET_USER_PASSWORD` with `mode: RESET_LINK`. The response shape is kept; if the email is not sent a temporary password is set and returned once (the previous manual fallback, `mode: TEMPORARY_PASSWORD_FALLBACK`). Account emails history labels the link.

## Change Log

- **2026-11-15 (Damage report record page and New invoice panel):** damage page rebuilt as a record page (progress, fact tiles, item cards with originals and marked-up copies, estimate total with coverage and "not estimated", decision rail with tier C send back and tier A release / take back / close without releasing / reopen, client preview from the client serializer, history, phone layout); new release message `client.damage_released` through the office pipeline with explicit transports (inbox + email default, SMS off; owner default pending); New invoice panel for the three kinds with a per-job preview from the generator's own functions, in-place rate fixes, optional "not billed: no rate", period default from the last invoice, idempotent create; batch stays beside it. No schema change. See "Damage report record page and New invoice panel".

- **2026-11-15 (Xero stays connected):** one token service for every Xero call: renewal 5 minutes before expiry, on a 401 (renew once, retry once) and daily by the new `xero-token-keepalive` job (so an idle connection never reaches the 60-day refresh-token expiry); single flight across web and worker by compare-and-set on `tokenVersion`; new tokens stored encrypted (previously plaintext) before use; transient failures retried and kept CONNECTED, terminal ones (invalid_grant, credentials refused, no refresh token, organisation removed) marked NEEDS_RECONNECT with a reason, kept for audit, with one inbox-only notice to administrators (`xero.reconnect_needed`). Settings › Xero shows connected since, last and next refresh, keep-alive, the 60-day limit, the reason and Reconnect; a connection without a refresh token says "Reconnect Xero once to keep it connected". Migration `20261115050000_xero_token_lifecycle`. Owner must set `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and reconnect once.

- **2026-11-15 (AI configuration page rebuilt):** one AI page at `/v2/admin/ai` with a status strip, Where AI runs (provider cards with tone bands, tests, keys confirmed with the person's own PIN), What AI does (per-feature rows, blocked and limit-hit states), Photo checks, Usage and cost ("Not known", never $0), Privacy and safety, a first-run guide and the phone layout; Settings › AI and the Ollama tab redirect to it; operations managers read it with the AI tools pack, without key hints; settings GET adds recorded test, provider-health, limit-hit and last-save facts. ### 2026-09-09: Cleaner draft acknowledgement and mutation locking

Draft PATCH performs active-assignment and existing job-lock checks plus shared read/merge/save under a per-job READ COMMITTED transaction/advisory lock. Save and clear helpers participate in the same protocol, including submit cleanup. Same-editor replacement and cross-editor merging remain unchanged. The broader submit workflow is not made atomic by this change. Draft API responses are private/no-store with sanitized unexpected errors.

The v2 workspace validates server save acknowledgements and displays pending, acknowledged or error states with an explicit retry. Immutable saves queue FIFO; edits invalidate old indicators, submit clears pending work, and unmount suppresses queued dispatch. Local edits mirror before network debounce. Workspace mounts are keyed by effective cleaner and job. Local recovery remains job-keyed and is not yet a durable actor/form-scoped upload queue; interrupted server outcomes and full submit integration remain open verification gates in the execution tracker.

Initial restoration now fails explicitly without enabling autosave when the shared draft read fails or is malformed. Stale responses cannot hydrate over newer state. Refresh failures preserve mounted controls only for transient errors; authorization denial clears content and pending saves. Verification includes 131 focused tests and four rollback-only checks against local PostgreSQL; browser/device and durable queue gates remain separate.

### 2026-09-09: Evidence upload receipt integrity

The shared v2 capture pipeline preserves successful receipts when temporary video cleanup fails, validates direct/multipart key and URL strings before returning attachments, and does not automatically retry failed videos based on their compressed size. Explicit recovery is still required for incomplete receipts. The existing IndexedDB draft helper is not yet wired into v2 capture; durable cross-navigation recovery remains unfinished.

Property access reads filter stored entries by the existing cleaner/laundry audience rules before projecting display fields. This prevents projection from turning restricted entries into implicitly shared entries. The daily cleaner briefing fallback and image-presence indicator use the same predicate. Existing property assignment/team authorization and legacy shared-entry behavior are unchanged. Pre-arrival change summaries remain pending a reliable historical baseline; current values are not evidence of changes since a visit.

Review corrections keep invalid early-arrival overrides unconfirmed instead of substituting a later standard arrival, validate detail-banner times, show finish-only planned times in Jobs, and include timing on the Drive next-stop panel. Route estimation anchors on first-stop access where known; reordering rejects a newly affected deadline even if the total missed-deadline count stays unchanged. These are advisory local route calculations, not scheduling mutations or verified travel-provider estimates.

Cleaner Today, Jobs, Calendar, job-detail banners, route timeline and inline Drive mode use a shared planned/guest timing summary. Explicit early arrival overrides standard same-day arrival, matching existing arrival rules. Late checkout and guest deadlines constrain route estimates; contradictions are advisory and do not rewrite schedules. Route page/API now use Sydney day boundaries with strict explicit-date validation, private API errors and an explicit page retry state. Assignment ownership remains enforced and raw internal notes remain server-side. See wave 17 of the execution tracker for tests and incomplete visual/type-check gates.

- **2026-08-24** — **Assistants become first-class accounts in the admin portal: a directory, admin-editable permissions, and an activity trail that actually has entries.** Three gaps, one shape. (1) The accounts page could CREATE assistants but never LIST them — the assistants tab held only the client-scoped invite manager, so a VA onboarded last month appeared nowhere unless you remembered which client they belonged to, while every other account type got a flat list. `components/v2/admin/accounts/va-directory.tsx` is that list: every VA across every client with client/team/grant context, the SAME account menu every other row gets (edit, reset password, reset 2FA, delete — `/api/admin/users/[id]/*` was always role-agnostic), a Profile link, and a stranded-login warning for a VA with no team (an input with no output: a login that can access nothing). The users GET now returns `vaTeam` (null for everyone else). (2) **An assistant's grants were editable only by the CLIENT they act for** — admin va-invites had GET+POST only, so the admin who onboarded a team could not correct its permissions without asking the client. New `PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/va-invites/[teamId]` reuses `updateVaTeam`/`deleteVaTeam` (one implementation, three doors: client portal, admin, and the invite flow) and writes an AuditLog row with the before-image — "who widened this team, from what" is the question an audit exists to answer. The invite-flow rule stands: adding a member still never rewrites grants. The directory carries the editor (grants, property scope, team active), and the admin profile page gains a "Delegated access" card for VAs — previously it rendered a VA as a strangely empty cleaner. (3) **The activity feed existed but VA rows were near-empty**: of 28 mutating client-portal handlers, only the four va-team routes audited. Every VA-REACHABLE mutating handler now writes an AuditLog row through `auditClientPortalAction` — booking, cases (create + update), maintenance, messages, cancel/reschedule/skip requests (+ skip withdrawal), light requests, task requests (create/update/withdraw), preferred cleaner (set/clear) — 14 handlers across 12 routes, each after the mutation succeeds, each carrying the actor label so the feed reads "did X for client Y". The 12 `requireRole([CLIENT])`-only mutating routes were deliberately NOT converted: a VA cannot reach them (paying invoices is on the VA forbidden list), and widening guards is a permission decision, not a logging one. One pre-existing trap found on the way: `preferred-cleaner/route.ts` holds TWO portal contexts (`portal0` is the real one); the audit initially pointed at the wrong one and tsc caught it. **No migration.**

- **2026-08-24** — **Job hours could be set but never cleared — plus a correction to what the recurring-hours fix claimed.** `estimatedHours` was `z.number().positive().optional()`, so a blank box sent `undefined`, and the PATCH route builds its Prisma payload with `const data = { ...body }` — an absent key is not an instruction to clear, it is no instruction at all, so the old value survived every attempt to remove it. Now `.nullable().optional()`, matching `fixedPrice` two lines below, which had used exactly that convention for a clearable field the whole time. Both form call sites send `null` instead of `undefined`; the CREATE route coerces back to `undefined`, where null and undefined both honestly mean "not set". Zero is still rejected: a 0 is an empty box everywhere in this codebase and null is how you say "empty" here, so accepting both would give one meaning two spellings. **THE CORRECTION:** the entry above for `lib/ops/recurring.ts` said a job created with no hours "was worth nothing to whoever cleaned it". That overstates it. `computeCleanerPay` deliberately falls back to the cleaner's CLOCKED timer hours when no allocated time is set — documented as "never fabricate hours" — so such a job pays the time actually worked, and pays nothing only if the cleaner also never clocked in. The recurring fix was still right (allocated time is the intended basis, and clocked time can differ from it), but the severity as written was wrong. - **2026-08-24** — **QA transport allowance, paid once per day worked.** Completing the owner's answer *"admin sets QA pay rate + transport allowance per day"*. **The RATE half already existed** — `qaPay.defaultMode/defaultFixedAmount/defaultHourlyRate/defaultHoursPerInspection` in settings, read by `computeQaAssignmentPay`, editable in the Safeguards settings section. Only the allowance was missing. **PER DAY IS THE WHOLE POINT:** an inspector visiting four properties on a Tuesday made ONE journey, and paying per inspection would be paying for journeys nobody made. **The day is a `Australia/Sydney` calendar day**, not a UTC one — an inspection finishing at 8pm Tuesday Sydney and one at 11am Wednesday are 09:00 and 01:00 UTC, so a naive UTC date either files them together or splits one evening across two days; either way the count is wrong, and the count IS the money. **CLAIMED, NOT DERIVED.** New `QaDayAllowance` table with `@@unique([inspectorId, day])`: deriving the allowance from whichever inspections sit on the invoice being built breaks the moment a day is SPLIT across two invoices — the payee excludes one inspection, sends the rest, then bills the last one next fortnight, and Tuesday's travel is paid twice. The row is created inside the send transaction (`createMany` + `skipDuplicates`, so a race becomes "already claimed" rather than a failed send) and stamped with the invoice id, which is what lets a VOID hand it back — a voided invoice that kept its claim would leave the day permanently unpayable, since the unique constraint means nothing else could ever claim it either. `amount` is snapshotted at claim time so a later rate change cannot re-price an invoice somebody already holds. The allowance gets its OWN section on the PDF, one line per day, each naming the day: a charge visible only in the total is a charge the payee cannot check. Rules are pure in `lib/finance/qa-transport.ts` (16 tests, including the Sydney-midnight straddle and the split-day exclusion). **NEEDS A MIGRATION:** `20260824000000_qa_day_allowance` (a new table only, additive). *Correction to an earlier note: this log previously implied the QA default rate was unbuilt. It was not — only the allowance was.*

- **2026-08-23** — **MULTI-ROLE USERS.** One person, more than one job — a cleaner who also inspects, a laundry driver who also cleans. Until now that meant two logins or a role describing half of what somebody does. New `UserRole` join table; **`User.role` stays the PRIMARY** and does not move, because it decides which portal somebody lands in, every historical row was written against it, and turning it into an array would have meant rewriting **848 authorisation call sites** in one change. An account with no extra roles behaves byte-for-byte as it did before — a test asserts that equivalence across all eight roles. **THE CENTRAL SPLIT:** *"May I?"* is authorisation, answered against every role a person HOLDS — somebody who genuinely is a QA inspector is one whichever hat they have on, and refusing them until they flick a switch adds no safety (it is one click) while breaking every cross-portal link. *"Where am I?"* is presentation, answered against the ACTIVE role — which portal, which nav, where home goes. `requireRole` takes the first; middleware's portal gates take the first; landing and nav take the second. **The active-role cookie is deliberately UNSIGNED and never trusted as a grant**: it names a role, and `resolveActiveRole` re-checks it against what the database says on every request, falling back to the primary when it does not match — which is also the revocation path, immediate rather than at next sign-in. The contrast with `sneek.test-as` is the point: that ticket IS authority (it names a user to become) so it is a signed JWE; this one names a role its holder must independently be proven to have, so signing it would protect nothing and imply a trust the code does not extend. `validate-session` and `requireSession` resolve **identically** — disagreement between them means middleware routes to one portal while the page there refuses, a redirect loop and a total outage. Granting is ADMIN-only (not OPS_MANAGER — it is a permission change), refuses ADMIN/OPS_MANAGER as secondary hats (privilege escalation), refuses the client-scoped roles, and writes its audit row INSIDE the transaction: a permission change that cannot be traced should not stand. **Three multi-role breaks fixed with it:** `payeeRole` was copied from `User.role` and frozen into the invoice snapshot at send time, so a mixed cleaner/QA invoice would have pushed to Xero with **every line labelled as one kind of work** — lines are now tagged with their source at send time and the kind is derived from the invoice's actual contents (`lib/invoicing/payee-kind.ts`, 12 tests); the maintenance candidate queries matched primary role only and would have rejected somebody whose second job qualified them, while telling them the opposite; and the nav badge counted every assignment while its link pointed at one role's section. **NEEDS A MIGRATION:** `20260823150000_user_extra_roles` (a new table only, additive). **Known remaining:** `lib/finance/payroll.ts:29` still scans `where: { role: CLEANER }` — partly compensated by `extraPayees`, which derives from real assignment ids rather than role, and that is the pattern to copy.

- **2026-08-23** — **The self-review failsafe was guarding the wrong table.** The owner's rule is explicit: *"add a fail safe to not to assign the cleans they do and do the QA themselves. never allows this."* `mayAssignQa` implemented it for `MaintenanceItemAssignment` — a person given the QA hat on a maintenance ITEM. The rail that actually inspects and SCORES a clean is `QaAssignment`, and it had no guard on **any** of its six write paths. **Not exploitable today**, and worth stating plainly rather than dressing up: job assignment requires `role: Role.CLEANER` (`app/api/admin/jobs/[id]/assign/route.ts:79`) and QA pickup requires QA_INSPECTOR/OPS_MANAGER/ADMIN, which are disjoint sets, so no account can currently sit on both sides. New `lib/qa/self-review.ts` (pure predicate + a thin DB assert, 11 tests) is called from all six: admin assign, admin **reassign** (guarding only the first assignment leaves the rule one edit from being bypassed), and the four self-claim paths — `pickup`, `timer`, `checkin` and `self-rework`. **The self-claim paths are the ones that matter**: `pickup` creates an assignment out of nothing, so guarding only the admin routes would leave the rule bypassable by walking up and claiming an inspection instead of waiting to be given one. `self-rework` is guarded because that is where the chain ends in MONEY — its `loadContext` accepts an assignment with `assignedToId: null`, so a caller need never have claimed the inspection to reach it, and could otherwise flag their own work and claim time and pay for putting it right.
